knowledge_statements.statement_title: Antiblockers and conformal hypergraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the hypergraph antiblocker and conformality, records the clique characterization and closure invariance, and preserves the failure of double-antiblocker involution in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a hypergraph \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\), the antiblocker \(a(H)\) is the hypergraph on \(V\) whose edges are the inclusionwise maximal stable sets of \(H\). Hence \(a(H)\) is a clutter, \(\alpha(H)=r_{\max}(a(H))\), and \(a(H)\) is conformal. A hypergraph \(H\) is conformal if, for every \(U\subseteq V\), whenever every pair of vertices in \(U\) is contained in some edge of \(H\), the whole set \(U\) is contained in an edge of \(H\). Moreover, \(H\), \(H^{\max}\), and \(H^{\downarrow}\) are conformal simultaneously, and this is equivalent to the existence of a graph on \(V\) whose inclusionwise maximal cliques are precisely the edges of \(H^{\max}\). Double antiblocking is not involutive for arbitrary hypergraphs: for the triangle hypergraph \(K_3\), \(a(a(K_3))=(V,\{V\})\ne K_3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The antiblocker has the maximal stable sets as its edges and is always a conformal clutter. Conformality means that any vertex set whose pairs are each contained in edges is itself contained in one edge. It is unchanged by maximal-edge reduction or downward closure and is equivalent to representing the maximal edges as the maximal cliques of a graph. Without an additional hypothesis, applying the antiblocker twice need not recover the original hypergraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a(H)\text{ is a conformal clutter},\quad \alpha(H)=r_{\max}(a(H)),\quad H\text{ conformal}\iff H^{\max}\text{ conformal}\iff H^{\downarrow}\text{ conformal},\quad H\text{ conformal}\iff \exists G\text{ on }V\text{ whose maximal cliques are }\mathcal E(H^{\max}).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Functional upper bound for a weighted hypergraph transversal number
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds the transversal number of a vertex-parallelized hypergraph using a superadditive, locally integral, locally homogeneous function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\) be a hypergraph, \(w:V\to\mathbb Z_+\), and \(f:\mathbb Z_+^V\to\mathbb R_+\). Assume \(f(x+y)\ge f(x)+f(y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb Z_+^V\); \(f(u)\in\mathbb Z_+\) whenever \(u\le w\); \(f(2x)=2f(x)\) whenever \(x\le w+\mathbf 1\); and \(f(\chi^U)>0\) for every \(U\in\mathcal E\). Then \(\tau(H^w)\le f(w)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If f is superadditive, integer-valued below w, doubles exactly for vectors below w plus the all-ones vector, and is positive on every hyperedge incidence vector, then the transversal number of the w-parallelization of H is at most f(w).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau(H^w)\le f(w)

children.title: Covering Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Incidence-specific strengthening families derived from covering structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^Tx\ge b\) is a covering inequality when \(a\in\mathbb R_+^n\), \(b>0\), and it is valid for \(X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard nonnegative valid inequalities for a binary covering set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricts to nonnegative inequalities valid for a binary covering set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A covering inequality for \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\ge\mathbf1\}\) is an inequality \(a^Tx\ge b\) with \(a\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(b>0\) that is valid for every \(x\in X\). Its support is \(S=\{i:a_i>0\}\); positive rescaling does not change the represented inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering inequality is a valid lower-bound inequality with nonnegative coefficients for a binary set-covering feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Covering Inequality Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a coherent local definition of nonnegative valid covering inequalities, but the convention is unsupported by a citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Pitch-Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Covering strengthenings organized by pitch.

assumptions_latex: \(a^Tx\ge b\) is a covering inequality with \(b>0\).
Its positive coefficients, counted with multiplicity, are \(a_{(1)}\le\cdots\le a_{(s)}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{pitch}(a,b)=\min\{k\in\{1,\ldots,s\}:\sum_{j=1}^k a_{(j)}\ge b\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard pitch definition for nonnegative covering inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite pitch by the smallest coefficients; inequalities with insufficient total coefficient have infinite pitch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pitch of \(a^Tx\ge b\) is the least \(k\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\) such that the sum of its \(k\) smallest positive coefficients is at least \(b\). If \(\sum_{j=1}^s a_{(j)}<b\), set \(\operatorname{pitch}(a,b)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pitch is the fewest smallest positive coefficients whose sum reaches the inequality's right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.title: Pitch-Inequality Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered-coefficient definition, including the infinite-pitch convention, is internally precise, but no source establishes the intended pitch convention.

children.title: Low-Pitch Regimes
children.top_down_role: Pitch-bounded families used for structured covering relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Pitch Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes pitch-one and pitch-at-most-two regimes directly from ordered positive coefficients, including singleton support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the \(s\ge1\) positive coefficients be ordered as \(a_{(1)}\le\cdots\le a_{(s)}\). The inequality has pitch one exactly when \(a_{(1)}\ge b\). It has pitch at most two exactly when either \(a_{(1)}\ge b\), or \(s\ge2\) and \(a_{(1)}+a_{(2)}\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pitch one occurs exactly when the smallest positive coefficient reaches the right-hand side. Pitch at most two occurs when this already holds or when at least two positive coefficients exist and the two smallest reach the right-hand side together.
assumptions_latex: \(a^Tx\ge b\) is a covering inequality of finite pitch.
Its \(s\ge1\) positive coefficients are ordered as \(a_{(1)}\le\cdots\le a_{(s)}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{pitch}(a,b)=1\iff a_{(1)}\ge b\), and \(\operatorname{pitch}(a,b)\le2\iff [a_{(1)}\ge b]\lor[s\ge2\land a_{(1)}+a_{(2)}\ge b]\).

notation.meaning: The positive coefficients in nondecreasing order.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: immediate characterization of the first two levels of the standard pitch hierarchy
source required for hierarchy terminology and conventions

children.title: Pitch Hierarchy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of fixed-pitch strengthening across covering instances.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge n\) is valid for \(X_n\) and has pitch \(n\).

notation.meaning: A binary covering set whose unique point is the all-ones vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit family demonstrates that valid covering inequalities have unbounded pitch
source required for any stronger hierarchy-completeness interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows unbounded pitch only; it does not assert extension-complexity or separation lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X_n=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x_i\ge1\text{ for every }i\}\), the valid covering inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge n\) has \(n\) positive coefficients, all equal to one, and therefore has pitch \(n\). Consequently, no fixed pitch bound contains every valid covering inequality across all dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid covering inequalities can have arbitrarily large pitch, so no dimension-independent fixed pitch level contains them all.

children.title: Conflict Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening based on incompatible pairs or conflict structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise conflict inequalities for binary incidence formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\), let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^V\) contain \(X\), and let \(G=(V,E)\) satisfy \(x_u+x_v\le 1\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(\{u,v\}\in E\). Define \[P'=P\cap\bigcap_{\{u,v\}\in E}\{x\in\mathbb R^V:x_u+x_v\le 1\}.\] Then \(X\subseteq P'\subseteq P\). Moreover, \(P'\subsetneq P\) if and only if some \(y\in P\) violates an edge inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding all valid pairwise conflict inequalities preserves every feasible binary vector and produces a relaxation contained in the original one. The containment is strict exactly when the original relaxation contains a point violating such an inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) satisfies \(x_u+x_v\le1\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(\{u,v\}\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\subseteq P'\subseteq P\), with \(P'\subsetneq P\) exactly when some \(y\in P\) violates an edge inequality.

notation.meaning: A linear relaxation containing all feasible incidence vectors.
A valid conflict graph on the binary variables.
The relaxation obtained by adding all edge inequalities.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid conflict inequalities preserve the integer feasible family while restricting its relaxation

children.title: Clique Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening based on mutually incompatible collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique cuts for binary variables represented as stable sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a valid conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\), and let \(Q\subseteq V\) be a clique of \(G\). Then \[\sum_{v\in Q}x_v\le1\] is valid for \(X\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\). For \(|Q|\ge3\), it implies every edge inequality internal to \(Q\) and is strictly stronger than their conjunction over \([0,1]^Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible solution selects at most one vertex of a conflict-graph clique. For a clique of at least three vertices, its clique inequality is strictly stronger than the internal edge inequalities over the unit cube.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a valid conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{v\in Q}x_v\le1\) is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\).

notation.meaning: A set of pairwise adjacent conflict-graph vertices.
The convex hull of feasible incidence vectors.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a stable set contains at most one vertex of a clique

children.title: Conflict-Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Graph interfaces used to expose incompatibility within set-system formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Graph Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical pairwise-conflict representation of a binary feasible family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\), define \(G_X=(V,E_X)\) by \[E_X=\bigl\{\{u,v\}\subseteq V:u\ne v\text{ and }x_u+x_v\le1\text{ for every }x\in X\bigr\}.\] Then every support \(S(x)=\{v\in V:x_v=1\}\), with \(x\in X\), is a stable set of \(G_X\), so \[X\subseteq\{\chi^S:S\text{ is a stable set of }G_X\}.\] Equality holds if and only if every stable set of \(G_X\) is feasible for the original incidence system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two variables are adjacent when no feasible solution selects both. Every feasible support is stable in this graph, and equality with the stable-set family holds exactly when pairwise conflicts capture all feasibility restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\subseteq\{\chi^S:S\text{ is a stable set of }G_X\}\).

notation.meaning: The conflict graph induced by the feasible family.
The incidence vector of a vertex subset.
The support of a binary vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: binary pairwise incompatibilities are represented by graph edges

children.title: Beyond-Clique Conflict Structures
children.top_down_role: Conflict-based strengthenings not captured by clique families alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Beyond-Clique Conflict Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd-cycle inequalities as a basic strengthening beyond clique cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a valid conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\), and let \(C\) be a simple odd cycle of length \(2k+1\), where \(k\ge2\). Then \[\sum_{v\in V(C)}x_v\le k\] is valid for \(X\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\). This inequality is not implied by the cycle-edge inequalities over \([0,1]^{V(C)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordless or non-chordless odd conflict cycle of length 2k+1, at most k cycle vertices can be selected. The resulting inequality is not implied by the cycle-edge constraints alone.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a valid conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\).
\(C\) is a simple odd cycle of length \(2k+1\), with \(k\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{v\in V(C)}x_v\le k\) is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\).

notation.meaning: A simple odd cycle in the conflict graph.
The vertex set of the cycle.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the stability number of an odd cycle of length 2k+1 is k

children.title: Partitioning Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening families exploiting exact-assignment structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioning Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rounded aggregation of binary set-partitioning equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfy \(Ax=\mathbf1\), and define \(R_j=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:A_{ij}=1\}\). For every \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the inequality \[\sum_{j=1}^n\left\lfloor\frac{|S\cap R_j|}{2}\right\rfloor x_j\le\left\lfloor\frac{|S|}{2}\right\rfloor\] is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every subset of partitioning rows, rounded half-incidence coefficients define a valid inequality for all binary set-partitioning solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^n\left\lfloor |S\cap R_j|/2\right\rfloor x_j\le\left\lfloor |S|/2\right\rfloor\).

notation.meaning: The set of rows covered by column j.
A selected subset of partitioning rows.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: integer rounding of an aggregation of partitioning equations yields the displayed valid inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Subset-Row Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical subset-row inequality for binary set-packing systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfy \(Ax\le\mathbf1\), and define \(R_j=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:A_{ij}=1\}\). For every \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the subset-row inequality \[\sum_{j=1}^n\left\lfloor\frac{|S\cap R_j|}{2}\right\rfloor x_j\le\left\lfloor\frac{|S|}{2}\right\rfloor\] is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every subset of packing rows, rounded half-incidence coefficients define a valid inequality for all binary set-packing solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^n\left\lfloor |S\cap R_j|/2\right\rfloor x_j\le\left\lfloor |S|/2\right\rfloor\).

notation.meaning: The set of rows containing column j.
The row subset used to form the inequality.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: counting incidences and integer rounding yields the subset-row inequality

children.title: Odd-Subset Row Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Subset Row Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd-cardinality specialization of subset-row inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfy \(Ax\le\mathbf1\), and let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfy \(|S|=2k+1\) for some \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). Then the subset-row inequality has the form \[\sum_{j=1}^n\left\lfloor\frac{|S\cap R_j|}{2}\right\rfloor x_j\le k.\] Its left-hand side is nonzero only if some column meets at least two rows of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an odd subset of 2k+1 packing rows, the subset-row right-hand side equals k. A nonzero coefficient occurs only for a column meeting at least two selected rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^n\left\lfloor |S\cap R_j|/2\right\rfloor x_j\le k\).

notation.meaning: The set of rows containing column j.
The half-size parameter of the odd row subset.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: odd cardinality specializes the rounded right-hand side to k

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioning–Packing Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity transfer of subset-row cuts between common-matrix partitioning and packing models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), define \(X_{=}=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax=\mathbf1\}\) and \(X_{\le}=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\le\mathbf1\}\), and for \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) define \[H_S=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\sum_{j=1}^n\left\lfloor\frac{|S\cap R_j|}{2}\right\rfloor x_j\le\left\lfloor\frac{|S|}{2}\right\rfloor\right\}.\] Then \(X_{=}\subseteq X_{\le}\subseteq H_S\). Validity therefore transfers from the common-matrix packing family to the partitioning family; facetness need not transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning solutions are packing solutions for the same incidence matrix, so every packing-valid subset-row inequality is also valid for the partitioning model. Facetness need not transfer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_{=}\subseteq X_{\le}\subseteq H_S\).

notation.meaning: The binary set-partitioning and set-packing feasible families.
The set of rows containing column j.
The halfspace defined by the subset-row inequality for S.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Greedy Set Cover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted greedy set cover with the universe-size harmonic guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U
e\varnothing\) be finite, let \(\mathcal S\subseteq2^U\) cover \(U\), and let \(c_S>0\) for every \(S\in\mathcal S\). Initialize \(C=\varnothing\) and \(R=U\). While \(R
e\varnothing\), choose \[S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\in\mathcal S:\,S\cap R
e\varnothing} rac{c_S}{|S\cap R|},\] set \(C\leftarrow C\cup\{S^*\}\), and set \(R\leftarrow R\setminus S^*\). The output \(C\) is a set cover satisfying \[\sum_{S\in C}c_S\le H_{|U|}\,\mathrm{OPT}\le(1+\ln|U|)\mathrm{OPT}.\] Ties may be resolved by any fixed deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty finite universe, repeatedly select a set of minimum cost per newly covered element. The resulting cover costs at most the |U|-th harmonic number times optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{S\in C}c_S\le H_{|U|}\,\mathrm{OPT}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cost-effectiveness and element prices in greedy set cover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions used by the weighted greedy set-cover algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an iteration with covered elements \(C\subseteq U\), the cost-effectiveness of a set \(S\) that covers at least one new element is \(c(S)/|S\setminus C|\). When \(S\) is selected, each newly covered element \(e\in S\setminus C\) receives the price \(\operatorname{price}(e)=c(S)/|S\setminus C|\), equivalently distributing \(c(S)\) equally among those elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set's cost-effectiveness is its cost divided by the number of new elements it covers. If selected, that average cost becomes the price of each newly covered element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{price}(e)=\frac{c(S)}{|S\setminus C|}\quad\text{for every }e\in S\setminus C\text{ when }S\text{ is selected}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted greedy set-cover algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy selection by minimum weight per newly covered element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(I\gets\varnothing\) and \(\widehat S_j\gets S_j\) for every \(j\). While the sets indexed by \(I\) do not cover the universe, choose \[\ell\in\arg\min_{j:\widehat S_j\neq\varnothing}\frac{w_j}{|\widehat S_j|},\] set \(I\gets I\cup\{\ell\}\), and update \(\widehat S_j\gets\widehat S_j\setminus S_\ell\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with no selected sets. Repeatedly choose a set minimizing its weight per currently uncovered element, then remove the newly covered elements from every residual set.

\(\bigcup_j S_j\) is the universe to be covered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is the index set returned when the selected sets form a cover.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Element-price bound for greedy set cover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-element price bound underlying the harmonic approximation analysis of weighted greedy set cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=|U|\), and number the elements \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) in the order in which the greedy set-cover algorithm covers them, resolving simultaneous-coverage ties arbitrarily. With prices assigned by that algorithm and \(\mathrm{OPT}\) denoting the cost of an optimal set cover, for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \[\operatorname{price}(e_k)\leq\frac{\mathrm{OPT}}{n-k+1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order the elements by when greedy set cover covers them, breaking simultaneous ties arbitrarily. The price of the kth element is at most the optimal cover cost divided by the number of elements in positions k through n.
assumptions_latex: (e_1,\ldots,e_n)\text{ is ordered by greedy coverage time, with ties resolved arbitrarily}
\operatorname{price}(e)\text{ is assigned by the weighted greedy set-cover algorithm}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\quad\operatorname{price}(e_k)\leq\frac{\mathrm{OPT}}{n-k+1}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Harmonic approximation guarantee for greedy set cover

knowledge_statements.title: Frequency-Sensitive Covering Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP threshold rounding parameterized by maximum element frequency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R_+^n\), let \(x^*\ge0\) satisfy \(Ax^*\ge\mathbf1\), and let \[f=\max_{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}}|\{j:A_{ij}=1\}|\ge1.\] Define \[\widehat x_j=\begin{cases}1,&x_j^*\ge1/f,\\0,&x_j^*<1/f.\end{cases}\] Then \(A\widehat x\ge\mathbf1\) and \(c^\top\widehat x\le f\,c^\top x^*\). If \(x^*\) is an optimal solution of the covering LP, \(\widehat x\) is an \(f\)-approximate integral cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round each fractional cover variable at least 1/f to one, where f is the maximum number of sets containing an element. The result is a feasible cover whose cost is at most f times the fractional cost.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) is a set-cover incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\widehat x\ge\mathbf1\) and \(c^\top\widehat x\le f\,c^\top x^*\).

notation.meaning: The maximum number of available sets containing any element.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reciprocal-frequency threshold rounding yields an f-factor cover

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Maximum-Coverage Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-constrained unweighted maximum coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be finite, let \(\mathcal S\subseteq2^U\) be finite, and let \(k\in\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(1\le k\le|\mathcal S|\). Initialize \(I_0=\varnothing\) and \(C_0=\varnothing\). For \(t=0,\ldots,k-1\), choose \[S_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{S\in\mathcal S\setminus I_t}|S\setminus C_t|,\] and set \(I_{t+1}=I_t\cup\{S_t\}\) and \(C_{t+1}=C_t\cup S_t\). If \(\mathrm{OPT}_k\) is the maximum number of elements coverable by at most \(k\) sets, then \[|C_k|\ge\left(1-\left(1-\frac1k\right)^k\right)\mathrm{OPT}_k\ge(1-1/e)\mathrm{OPT}_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For 1≤k≤|S|, select k distinct sets successively by maximum marginal coverage. Their union covers at least 1-(1-1/k)^k, and hence at least 1-1/e, of the optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|C_k|\ge\bigl(1-(1-1/k)^k\bigr)\mathrm{OPT}_k\ge(1-1/e)\mathrm{OPT}_k\).

notation.meaning: The subfamily selected after t iterations.
The elements covered after t selections.
The maximum coverage obtainable with at most k sets.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: greedy maximization of a monotone coverage function has the classical 1-1/e guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximation Guarantee for Greedy Maximum Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-budget approximation guarantee for exact-marginal greedy maximum coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted maximum-coverage instance with nonnegative element weights and cardinality budget \(k\), let \(\mathrm{GREEDY}\) be the coverage obtained after \(k\) exact maximum-marginal choices and let \(\mathrm{OPT}\) be an optimal solution using \(k\) sets. Then \[\operatorname{wt}(\mathrm{GREEDY})\geq\left[1-\left(1-\frac1k\right)^k\right]\operatorname{wt}(\mathrm{OPT})>\left(1-\frac1e\right)\operatorname{wt}(\mathrm{OPT}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After k exact greedy selections, the covered weight is at least 1 minus (1 minus 1/k) to the kth power times optimum, and hence strictly more than a 1 minus 1/e fraction of optimum.
assumptions_latex: \mathrm{GREEDY}\text{ is produced by exact maximum-marginal selection for }k\text{ iterations}
\mathrm{OPT}\text{ is optimal among solutions using }k\text{ sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{wt}(\mathrm{GREEDY})\geq\left[1-\left(1-\frac1k\right)^k\right]\operatorname{wt}(\mathrm{OPT})>\left(1-\frac1e\right)\operatorname{wt}(\mathrm{OPT}).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R_+^n\), let \(x^*\ge0\) satisfy \(Ax^*\ge\mathbf1\), and let \[f=\max_{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}}|\{j:A_{ij}=1\}|\ge1.\] Define \(\widehat x\in\{0,1\}^n\) deterministically by \[\widehat x_j=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_j^*\ge1/f.\] Then \(A\widehat x\ge\mathbf1\) and \(c^\top\widehat x\le f\,c^\top x^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Randomized Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bernoulli rounding of a fractional incidence vector, including optional scaling and truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a fractional vector \(x\in[0,1]^n\) and a scale \(\lambda>0\), independently generate \(X_i\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\Pr[X_i=1]=p_i:=\min\{1,\lambda x_i\}\). Return the selected index set \(R:=\{i:X_i=1\}\). For every coefficient vector \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), linearity of expectation gives \(\mathbb E[a^\top X]=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i p_i\), irrespective of independence; independence additionally permits product formulas and concentration bounds for sums involving distinct coordinates. In a covering or packing application, choose \(\lambda\), and any subsequent alteration rule, so that constraint-violation probabilities and expected objective loss meet the required guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round each fractional coordinate independently to a Bernoulli variable, optionally after scaling; expectations are preserved according to the chosen probabilities, while independence enables concentration analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) and \(\mathbb E[a^\top X]=\sum_i a_i\min\{1,\lambda x_i\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard independent Bernoulli rounding scheme

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Randomized Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise dependent rounding for a box vector having integral coordinate sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in[0,1]^n\) satisfy \(\sum_i x_i=m\in\mathbb Z\). While two coordinates \(x_i,x_j\) are fractional, consider \(x+t(e_i-e_j)\) and let \(t^+>0\) and \(t^-<0\) be the maximal steps retaining membership in \([0,1]^n\). Replace \(x\) by the positive endpoint with probability \(-t^-/(t^+-t^-)\), and by the negative endpoint with probability \(t^+/(t^+-t^-)\). Each update makes at least one chosen coordinate integral, preserves the coordinate sum deterministically, and preserves every coordinate in expectation. Return the resulting vector \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly move a pair of fractional coordinates to a random box endpoint, preserving their sum and individual expectations until an integral vector remains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(\sum_iX_i=\sum_ix_i\), and \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i\) for every \(i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and endpoint probabilities match the standard pairwise dependent-rounding construction. No specific source or locator supports the construction and its preservation properties. The update-invariant explanation is proof text and should not remain in the final knowledge statement.

children.title: Conditional-Expectation Derandomization
children.top_down_role: Deterministic counterparts obtained through conditional objective control.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Expectation Derandomization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential derandomization using an exactly computable conditional objective or pessimistic estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a randomized construction use variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with finite domains, and let \(Z\) be a real-valued cost to minimize. Assume every conditional expectation \(\mathbb E[Z\mid X_1=a_1,\ldots,X_i=a]\) can be computed. Starting with no assignments, at stage \(i\) choose a feasible value \(a_i\) minimizing this conditional expectation over the domain of \(X_i\). Output the complete assignment \((a_1,\ldots,a_n)\). Since the current conditional expectation is an average of the next-stage conditional expectations, the selected value never increases it; consequently the deterministic output has cost at most \(\mathbb E[Z]\). The same rule applies to a pessimistic estimator satisfying the corresponding averaging inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix random choices sequentially, always selecting a value that does not increase the conditional expected cost, thereby matching the original expectation deterministically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\leq \mathbb E[Z]\).

notation.meaning: cost or pessimistic estimator to minimize
deterministically fixed value of the ith variable

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical method of conditional expectations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but an authoritative source is absent and the exact formulation is not yet reliable. Choices must be restricted to values with positive conditional probability, or conditional expectations on null events must be defined. The pessimistic-estimator extension also needs its precise domination and averaging hypotheses. The averaging explanation is proof text.

children.title: Limited-Independence Derandomization

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Independence Derandomization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replacement of full independence by bounded-wise independence when analysis uses only low-order moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a randomized rounding analysis bounds a nonnegative badness variable \(Z\) using only joint moments of the rounding variables of total degree at most \(k\). If \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are replaced by variables having the same marginals and being \(k\)-wise independent, then every polynomial moment used by that analysis is unchanged. Hence any guarantee derived solely from those moments, such as \(\mathbb E[Z]\leq B\), remains valid. If the \(k\)-wise independent family is generated by a finite seed space and \(Z\), or a dominating pessimistic estimator, is evaluable for each seed, enumerating the seeds and returning the best outcome yields a deterministic outcome of value at most \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an analysis uses only moments through degree k, k-wise independence suffices; enumerating a finite seed family can then produce a deterministic outcome meeting the expectation bound.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\geq0\) is controlled only by moments of degree at most \(k\)
the replacement distribution preserves those moments
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Z]\leq B\) remains valid, and exhaustive seed selection yields \(Z\leq B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A principle is an appropriate role for this terminal container, but the exact claim needs a source. It should explicitly identify the fully independent reference distribution whose low-order joint moments are preserved and state that the seed distribution's average estimator value is at most B before concluding that exhaustive seed selection finds an outcome of value at most B.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Fitting for Set Cover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation certificate obtained by scaling an approximately feasible dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For weighted set cover on universe \(U\), with sets \(\mathcal S\) and costs \(c_S\geq0\), let \(C\subseteq\mathcal S\) cover \(U\). Suppose numbers \(y_e\geq0\) and \(\alpha\geq1\) satisfy \(\sum_{e\in S}y_e\leq\alpha c_S\) for every \(S\in\mathcal S\), and \(\sum_{S\in C}c_S\leq\sum_{e\in U}y_e\). Then \(y/\alpha\) is feasible for the dual of the standard fractional set-cover relaxation. Weak duality therefore gives \(\sum_{S\in C}c_S\leq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{LP}\leq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\), so \((C,y,\alpha)\) is a directly checkable \(\alpha\)-approximation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a cover is charged to nonnegative element weights violating each dual constraint by at most alpha, scaling the weights proves that the cover is an alpha-approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(C)\leq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{LP}\leq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: fitted dual weight of element e

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard dual-fitting certificate for weighted set cover

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role is well matched to dual fitting, and the stated inequalities do yield the claimed alpha-approximation certificate. No set-cover-specific source and locator are supplied, however. The weak-duality derivation is proof text and should be reduced to the certificate conditions and certified conclusion after sourcing.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Covering Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic primal–dual growth-and-selection scheme for nonnegative covering programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the covering program \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\geq b,\ x\geq0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\leq c,\ y\geq0\}\), where \(A,b,c\geq0\). Initialize \(x=0\) and \(y=0\). While a primal covering constraint is unsatisfied, increase its dual variable until some dual constraint becomes tight, then activate the associated primal variable according to the problem-specific selection rule. After all covering constraints are satisfied, optionally delete redundant activated variables in reverse order. Output the resulting feasible primal solution together with the dual vector; an approximation bound follows when the selection and deletion rules bound the primal cost charged to each dual contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raise dual variables for uncovered requirements until primal choices become tight, select those choices, and optionally prune them; bounded charging to the feasible dual gives an approximation guarantee.
assumptions_latex: the growth rule preserves \(A^\top y\leq c\)
the selection rule eventually produces \(Ax\geq b\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is primal feasible and \(y\) is dual feasible; any established charging factor \(\alpha\) implies \(c^\top x\leq\alpha b^\top y\leq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\).

children.title: LP-Based Packing Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding frameworks specialized to fractional set-packing solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: LP-Based Packing Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized rounding with alteration for a nonnegative packing relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an optimal fractional solution \(x\in[0,1]^n\) of \(\max\{w^\top x:Ax\leq b\}\), where \(A,b,w\geq0\), choose a scale \(\lambda\in(0,1]\). Independently set \(X_i=1\) with probability \(\lambda x_i\). If \(AX\nleq b\), apply a specified alteration map that changes selected coordinates only from \(1\) to \(0\) until every packing constraint is satisfied. Return the altered vector \(Y\). The output is always feasible when the alteration terminates correctly. Its approximation guarantee is determined by lower bounds on the survival probabilities \(\Pr[Y_i=1]\), since \(\mathbb E[w^\top Y]=\sum_iw_i\Pr[Y_i=1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale and independently round a fractional packing solution, then delete selected items causing violations; survival probabilities determine the expected approximation ratio.
assumptions_latex: the alteration map terminates with feasibility
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(AY\leq b\), and \(\mathbb E[w^\top Y]=\sum_iw_i\Pr[Y_i=1]\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard randomized rounding with alteration template

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the packing-rounding leaf, and the generic rounding-with-alteration template is coherent. No inspectable source supports the template or survival-probability guarantee. Because the alteration map and any quantitative survival bound are deliberately problem-specific, a source is needed to delimit the exact general claim.

children.title: Cover–Packing Relaxation Interface
children.top_down_role: Shared relaxation structure connecting LP-based covering and packing approaches.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover–Packing Relaxation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-duality interface between fractional covering and packing over a nonnegative incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R_+^n\). The fractional covering relaxation is \(P_C:=\min\{c^\top x:Ax\geq b,\ x\geq0\}\), while its packing dual is \(P_P:=\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\leq c,\ y\geq0\}\). Every feasible pair satisfies \(b^\top y\leq c^\top x\). If both programs are feasible and one has a finite optimum, finite-dimensional linear-programming strong duality yields attained optimal solutions \(x^*,y^*\) with \(c^\top x^*=b^\top y^*\). Thus feasible packing vectors provide lower bounds and charging certificates for rounded covering solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative covering LP has a packing dual; weak duality supplies lower bounds, and under feasibility and finiteness strong duality equates their optimal values.
assumptions_latex: the common optimal value is finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^\top y\leq c^\top x\) for feasible \(x,y\), and \(c^\top x^*=b^\top y^*\) at optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality role exactly fits the cover-packing interface, and the finite-dimensional primal-dual pair, weak-duality inequality, and strong-duality conclusion are correctly stated under the given feasibility and finiteness assumptions. No authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Set Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-weight-first greedy algorithm for weighted set packing with bounded set cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be a finite family of sets, each of cardinality at most \(k\), with weights \(w_S\geq0\). Initialize \(P:=\varnothing\) and \(R:=\mathcal S\). While \(R\neq\varnothing\), choose a set \(S\in R\) of maximum weight, add \(S\) to \(P\), and delete from \(R\) every set intersecting \(S\). Return \(P\). The selected sets are pairwise disjoint. Charging every optimal set to the first selected set that deletes it shows that at most \(k\) mutually disjoint optimal sets are charged to each selected set, each having no larger weight; hence \(w(P)\geq \operatorname{OPT}/k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose the heaviest remaining set and discard its conflicts. For sets of size at most k, the resulting packing is a k-approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is a set packing and \(w(P)\geq\operatorname{OPT}/k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard charging analysis for bounded-cardinality set packing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the terminal container, and maximum-weight-first greedy is a k-approximation for nonnegative weighted set packing when every set has cardinality at most k. An authoritative set-packing source is missing. The charging paragraph is proof text and should be omitted from a sourced replacement.

children.title: Local Search for Bounded-Cardinality Set Packing

knowledge_statements.title: Local Search for Bounded-Cardinality Set Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange local search using bounded-size improvements in a weighted set-packing instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be a finite family with \(|S|\leq k\) and weights \(w_S\geq0\), and let \(p\geq1\). Start with any packing \(P\subseteq\mathcal S\). While there exist disjoint subfamilies \(A\subseteq\mathcal S\setminus P\) and \(B\subseteq P\), with \(|A|+|B|\leq p\), such that \((P\setminus B)\cup A\) is a packing and \(w(A)>w(B)\), replace \(P\) by \((P\setminus B)\cup A\). Return \(P\) when no such exchange exists. With rational weights and strict improvement, a termination rule based on objective increase or explicit state avoidance yields a \(p\)-exchange local optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly replace a bounded number of chosen sets by a heavier compatible bounded family, stopping when no improving exchange of size at most p remains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is a packing admitting no improving exchange with \(|A|+|B|\leq p\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the local-search leaf, and the exchange condition correctly defines a p-exchange local optimum. A bounded-cardinality set-packing source with a precise locator is absent. Since the family is finite and every accepted exchange strictly increases weight, termination already follows without rational weights or an additional state-avoidance rule; a sourced formulation should remove that distracting qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmenting-Structure Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-graph structures whose exchange strictly improves a current set packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set family \(\mathcal S\) and a current packing \(P\subseteq\mathcal S\), define the conflict graph with one vertex for each set and an edge between intersecting sets. An augmenting structure relative to \(P\) is a pair \((A,B)\) with \(A\subseteq\mathcal S\setminus P\) and \(B\subseteq P\) such that the sets in \(A\) are pairwise disjoint, every neighbor in \(P\) of a set in \(A\) belongs to \(B\), and the exchange improves the objective: \(|A|>|B|\) in the unweighted case, or \(w(A)>w(B)\) in the weighted case. Replacing \(B\) by \(A\) therefore yields a strictly better packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmenting structure is a compatible entering family together with all conflicting chosen sets, where replacing the latter by the former strictly improves cardinality or weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((P\setminus B)\cup A\) is a packing with strictly larger cardinality or weight.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is an appropriate role for this container, and the conflict-neighborhood conditions make the exchange feasible. The term 'augmenting structure' varies across the set-packing literature, so a precise source is necessary. The weighted variant must also introduce the weight function and its domain explicitly before using w(A) and w(B).

children.title: Epsilon-Net Structures
children.top_down_role: Structural roles of epsilon-nets in geometric covering.

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Net Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted epsilon-nets for finite range spaces, with the uniform case as a specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\mathcal R)\) be a finite range space, let \(\mu:X\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfy \(\mu(X):=\sum_{x\in X}\mu(x)>0\), and let \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\). A subset \(N\subseteq X\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-net with respect to \(\mu\) if every range \(R\in\mathcal R\) having \(\mu(R):=\sum_{x\in R}\mu(x)\geq\varepsilon\mu(X)\) intersects \(N\). Equivalently, \(N\cap R=\varnothing\) implies \(\mu(R)<\varepsilon\mu(X)\). Under uniform weights, the condition becomes \(|R|\geq\varepsilon|X|\Rightarrow N\cap R\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-net intersects every range carrying at least an epsilon fraction of the total weight; uniform weights recover the usual cardinality definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-net exactly when \(\mu(R)\geq\varepsilon\mu(X)\) implies \(N\cap R\neq\varnothing\) for every \(R\in\mathcal R\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard weighted finite epsilon-net definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role exactly fits the epsilon-net structures leaf. The weighted finite-range-space definition, its contrapositive, and the uniform specialization are consistent, with all essential objects quantified. No authoritative epsilon-net source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Randomized Sampling Constructions
children.top_down_role: Sampling-based construction regimes for epsilon-nets.

assumptions_latex: \((X,\mathcal R)\) is a range space of VC dimension at most \(d\).
\(\mu\) is a probability measure on \(X\), and \(0<\varepsilon,\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-net with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Family of measurable ranges on the ground space
Independent random sample from the ground-space measure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-VC-dimension random sampling under an arbitrary probability measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, if \(N\) consists of \(m\) independent samples from \(\mu\) and \[m\geq \frac{C}{\varepsilon}\left(d\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon}+\log\frac{1}{\delta}\right),\] then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), every range \(R\in\mathcal R\) satisfying \(\mu(R)\geq\varepsilon\) intersects \(N\). Thus random sampling constructs an \(\varepsilon\)-net of size \(O((d\log(1/\varepsilon)+\log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently large independent sample hits every range having measure at least epsilon, with failure probability at most delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Sampling Constructions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-VC sampling theorem is standard and fits the randomized-construction leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The final big-O size claim requires choosing m at the threshold; it does not follow for every arbitrarily larger m. Measurability conditions for the ranges and sampling event should also be stated.

children.title: Deterministic Epsilon-Net Constructions
children.top_down_role: Deterministic counterparts to randomized epsilon-net construction.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(\mathcal R\subseteq 2^X\) are finite and explicitly listed.
An integer \(m\) is known for which an \(\varepsilon\)-net of size at most \(m\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enumeration returns an \(\varepsilon\)-net of cardinality at most \(m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite derandomization by exhaustive conditional search, not a polynomial-time geometric construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Enumerate subsets \(N\subseteq X\) in nondecreasing cardinality, stopping at the first subset with \(|N|\leq m\) such that \[N\cap R\neq\varnothing\qquad\text{for every }R\in\mathcal R\text{ with }|R|\geq\varepsilon|X|.\] Output that subset and report failure only after every subset of size at most \(m\) has been tested. Under the existence assumption, the algorithm terminates with a deterministic \(\varepsilon\)-net. Its direct implementation requires at most \(\sum_{j=0}^{m}\binom{|X|}{j}|\mathcal R|\) range-intersection tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate small subsets and return the first one hitting every range containing at least an epsilon fraction of the ground set.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Epsilon-Net Constructions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exhaustive enumeration is a valid deterministic algorithm for the explicitly finite setting and the algorithm kind fits the leaf. An authoritative locator is still required; the statement should not be interpreted as an efficient geometric derandomization.

assumptions_latex: A feasible solution \(F\) has additive nonnegative value \(w(F)\).
For an integer \(k\geq2\), every object is excluded by exactly one of \(k\) shifted decompositions.
Each residual instance decomposes into independently solvable bounded-locality components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The best shifted residual solution has value at least \((1-1/k)\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: Objects of an optimal solution removed by shift r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract maximization form of the shifting argument for geometric local-decomposition schemes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^*\) be optimal and let \(B_0,\ldots,B_{k-1}\) be its objects removed by the respective shifts. If these sets partition \(F^*\), then \[\sum_{r=0}^{k-1}w(B_r)=w(F^*)=\operatorname{OPT}.\] Hence some shift \(r\) satisfies \(w(B_r)\leq\operatorname{OPT}/k\). Solving every residual component optimally for each shift and returning the best union therefore produces a feasible solution of value at least \(\operatorname{OPT}-w(B_r)\geq(1-1/k)\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among k shifted decompositions, one removes at most a 1/k fraction of an optimal additive solution, yielding a local approximation scheme.
knowledge_statements.title: Shifting Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The averaging principle is plausible, but the record contains proof-style derivation and supplies no source for the partition, feasibility, and exact residual-solution hypotheses needed by this abstract shifting guarantee.

children.title: Geometric Separator Methods
children.top_down_role: Separator-based reductions for geometric covering or packing instances.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the conflict graph of a geometric instance.
A separator \(S\subseteq V\) leaves components \(V_1,\ldots,V_t\) with no edges between distinct components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixing the decisions on \(S\) separates the residual optimization into independent component subproblems.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic consequence of a valid separator; no universal geometric separator theorem is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each feasible assignment \(a\) to the objects represented by \(S\), restrict every component \(V_i\) by the compatibility conditions induced by \(a\). Because no conflict edge joins distinct components, feasible component solutions can then be combined, and for an additive objective the conditioned optimum satisfies \[\operatorname{OPT}(G\mid a)=w(a)+\sum_{i=1}^{t}\operatorname{OPT}(G[V_i]\mid a).\] Enumerating admissible assignments on \(S\) and selecting the best combined solution is therefore exact whenever the separator assignments are exhaustively represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After decisions on a geometric separator are fixed, disconnected conflict components can be optimized independently and their additive values combined.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Separator Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separator principle fits the leaf, but absence of intercomponent conflict edges yields independent subproblems only when the conflict graph completely represents feasibility and the objective decomposes as asserted. Those conditions and the displayed identity need source support.

children.title: Recursive Geometric Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical subdivision regimes for spatial instances.

assumptions_latex: Every nonterminal subinstance admits a separator and a finite set of boundary states.
Conditioned on a boundary state, the separator creates independent child subinstances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root table contains the exact optimum when all feasible boundary states are enumerated.

notation.meaning: Subinstance associated with a decomposition-tree node
Admissible boundary states at node u

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact recursion over separator states for additive geometric objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Build a rooted decomposition tree by repeatedly separating each nonterminal instance \(I_u\). For every node \(u\) and state \(\sigma\in\Sigma_u\), compute bottom-up \[D_u(\sigma)=\operatorname*{opt}_{\tau\text{ compatible with }\sigma}\left(w_u(\sigma,\tau)+\sum_{v\text{ child of }u}D_v(\tau|_v)\right).\] Initialize leaf entries by direct optimization, discard incompatible states, and output the best entry at the root. The procedure is exact if each feasible global solution induces an enumerated state at every separator and every compatible collection of child solutions can be combined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively separate the instance, tabulate every boundary state, combine compatible child optima, and return the best root entry.
knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Geometric Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-state recursion has the appropriate algorithm role, but its transition variables, local contribution, state restrictions, and combination property are only schematic. A source tied to a specific separator-state framework is needed.

children.title: Boundary Interaction Control
children.top_down_role: Treatment of objects crossing separator or decomposition boundaries.

assumptions_latex: A separator divides the instance into regions \(I_1,[0m\ldots,I_t\).
Every constraint involving objects from different regions contains at least one boundary object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Agreement on boundary traces is sufficient to certify compatibility of independently computed regional solutions.

notation.meaning: Set of objects meeting or crossing the separator boundary
Boundary trace of a regional solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency condition for finite boundary states in separator-based geometric optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A boundary representation is interaction-complete if, for any regional feasible solutions \(F_i\subseteq I_i\), the union \(\bigcup_iF_i\) is globally feasible exactly when their traces \(\partial F_i\subseteq B\) satisfy a designated compatibility predicate \(K(\partial F_1,\ldots,\partial F_t)\). Boundary interaction is controlled when this predicate is decidable from the traces alone and the number of attainable traces is finite. Under this condition, a decomposition algorithm need store only one best regional solution for each trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary control holds when regional solutions are globally compatible exactly when their finite separator traces satisfy a decidable compatibility predicate.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Interaction Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interaction-completeness condition fits the leaf, but the first assumption contains malformed text (`[0m\ldots`) and the boundary-object and trace models are not defined sufficiently to validate the claimed sufficiency. Object-specific source support is required.

children.title: Geometric Covering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric structures that specifically shape covering methods.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite set of demand points and \(\mathcal R\) is a family of geometric ranges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible covering solution is precisely a subfamily whose union contains every demand point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite weighted geometric set cover induced by point-range incidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The geometric covering problem induced by \((P,\mathcal R)\) is \[\min\left\{\sum_{R\in\mathcal R}c_Rx_R:\ \sum_{R\in\mathcal R:\,p\in R}x_R\geq1\ \text{for every }p\in P,\quad x_R\in\{0,1\}\right\}.\] Its regime is determined by the permitted geometric range class, such as disks, halfspaces, or axis-parallel rectangles, together with any restrictions on dimension, weights, and incidence representation. Feasibility requires every point of \(P\) to lie in at least one selected range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric covering selects minimum-cost ranges so that every demand point belongs to at least one selected range.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Covering Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation is the standard weighted geometric set-cover definition and fits the covering-regime leaf, but the range family must be declared finite for the displayed finite integer program as scoped, and no authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Geometric Packing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric structures that specifically shape packing methods.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal O\) is a finite family of geometric objects.
Each object \(O\) has nonnegative weight \(w_O\), and conflicts are represented by a symmetric relation \(\sim\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible packing is precisely a pairwise nonconflicting subfamily of \(\mathcal O\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite weighted geometric packing expressed through its conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The geometric packing problem induced by \((\mathcal O,\sim)\) is \[\max\left\{\sum_{O\in\mathcal O}w_Ox_O:\ x_O+x_{O'}\leq1\ \text{whenever }O\sim O',\quad x_O\in\{0,1\}\right\}.\] Typically \(O\sim O'\) means that the interiors intersect, although boundary-touching conventions must be fixed by the application. The regime is determined by the geometric object class, dimension, weights, and conflict convention. Its feasible solutions are independent sets of the associated conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric packing selects a maximum-weight subfamily of pairwise compatible objects, equivalently an independent set in the conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Packing Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conflict-graph packing formulation fits the leaf, but the conflict relation must apply only to distinct objects or be explicitly irreflexive. Under the stated interior-intersection convention an object intersects itself, which would otherwise impose 2x_O≤1 and forbid selection.

children.title: Exact Set-System Optimization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Only incidence-specific exact-solver interfaces are included; generic search machinery is external.

children.title: Constraint Generation for Implicit Set Systems

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Generation for Implicit Set Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite cutting-plane scheme for an implicit linear set-system formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite subset \(J_0\subseteq I\) and set \(J:=J_0\). At each iteration choose \[x^J\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{c^{\mathsf T}x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i\text{ for every }i\in J\}.\] Query the oracle at \(x^J\). If it returns a violated index \(i\in I\setminus J\), set \(J:=J\cup\{i\}\) and repeat. If it certifies \(x^J\in P\), output \(x^J\). Under the stated attainment assumption, the algorithm terminates after at most \(|I\setminus J_0|\) constraint additions, and its output minimizes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly optimize over the current finite constraint subset and add an oracle-identified violated constraint. If every restricted master encountered attains an optimum, the finite procedure terminates with an optimizer of the full linear relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite, \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i\text{ for every }i\in I\}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
For every constraint subset \(J\) encountered by the algorithm, the restricted linear program has an attained optimum.
An oracle returns a violated constraint for every queried \(x\notin P\), and certifies membership when \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates after finitely many constraint additions and returns an optimizer of \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\).

source_refs.source_title: A First Course in Combinatorial Optimization

assumptions_latex: A rational polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is described by an implicit family of valid incidence inequalities.
A separation oracle can optimize violation over that inequality family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive maximum violation supplies a valid separating cut; a nonpositive maximum certifies satisfaction of the entire family.

notation.meaning: Violation of inequality F at the query point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation over an incidence-indexed inequality family.

source_refs.locator: * 4.2 Optimization from Separation p. 105
Section 4.6. Separation and Optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a query point \(\bar x\), compute \[F^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{F}\ v_F(\bar x),\qquad v_F(\bar x):=a_F^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_F.\] If \(v_{F^*}(\bar x)>0\), then \(a_{F^*}^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_{F^*}\) is valid for \(P\) and violated by \(\bar x\), so it is a directly checkable separating cut. If \(v_{F^*}(\bar x)\leq0\), then \(\bar x\) satisfies every inequality in the indexed family. This conclusion concerns that family unless its completeness for \(P\) is separately established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize incidence-inequality violation; a positive optimum gives a separating cut, while a nonpositive optimum certifies satisfaction of the whole family.
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence-Specific Cut Separation

source_witnesses.locator: * 4.2 Optimization from Separation p. 105
Section 4.6. Separation and Optimization p. 93

children.title: Dynamic Programming on Structured Set Systems

assumptions_latex: The incidence structure has a rooted decomposition tree of finite width.
For each decomposition node, feasibility and objective contributions depend on the processed part only through a finite boundary state.
The objective is additive across introduced objects or incidences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The best accepting root state equals the global optimum.

notation.meaning: Finite state set at decomposition node t
Best partial value realizing state sigma

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite-state dynamic programming over a structured incidence decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Process the decomposition tree bottom-up. For every node \(t\) and state \(\sigma\in\Sigma_t\), set \[D_t(\sigma)=\operatorname*{opt}_{(\sigma_u)_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(t)}\text{ compatible with }\sigma}\left(g_t(\sigma,(\sigma_u)_u)+\sum_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(t)}D_u(\sigma_u)\right),\] using direct initialization at leaves and discarding unrealizable states. At the root \(r\), output the best value among accepting states and recover a solution through stored predecessor choices. Exactness follows from the assumption that boundary states preserve all information needed for extension and combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tabulate optimal partial solutions by finite boundary states along a decomposition tree, combine compatible child states, and read the optimum at the root.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Programming on Structured Set Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the dynamic-programming leaf, but the decomposition, states, compatibility relation, accepting states, and local contribution are schematic. A source for a concrete structured set-system decomposition is required.

children.title: Column Formulations for Set Systems
children.top_down_role: Set-covering, packing, and partitioning masters with implicit columns; generic decomposition theory and application-specific pricing algorithms remain external.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite set of covering requirements and \(\mathcal C\) is a possibly very large family of columns.
Column \(j\) has cost \(c_j\) and incidence coefficient \(a_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integer feasible master solutions are exactly the selected column families covering every requirement.

notation.meaning: Multiplicity or selection variable for column j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical large-column integer and linear set-covering master formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set-covering master is \[\min\left\{\sum_{j\in\mathcal C}c_jx_j:\ \sum_{j\in\mathcal C}a_{ij}x_j\geq1\text{ for every }i\in I,\quad x_j\in\mathbb Z_+\right\}.\] For single-use columns, replace \(x_j\in\mathbb Z_+\) by \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\). Replacing integrality by \(x_j\geq0\) gives the linear master relaxation. If \(\mathcal C\) is implicit, a restricted master uses \(\mathcal C'\subseteq\mathcal C\), while missing columns are detected through reduced-cost pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-covering master chooses minimum-cost columns so every requirement is covered at least once; relaxing integrality gives the linear master.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Covering Masters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and covering-master formulas fit the leaf. An authoritative source is missing, and the record should clarify whether the large column family is finite and whether costs are nonnegative when unrestricted integer multiplicities are allowed.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Packing Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary and linear-relaxation master formulations for selecting incidence-compatible columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite row set, \(P\) a finite column family, \(a_{ip}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether column \(p\) uses row \(i\), and \(c_p\in\mathbb R\). The set-packing master is \[\max\left\{\sum_{p\in P}c_p\lambda_p:\sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}\lambda_p\le 1\ \text{for every }i\in I,\ \lambda_p\in\{0,1\}\ \text{for every }p\in P\right\}.\] Its linear relaxation replaces \(\lambda_p\in\{0,1\}\) by \(0\le\lambda_p\le1\). Each row inequality permits that row to occur in at most one selected column in an integral solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-packing master selects profitable columns while allowing every incidence row to be used at most once; its LP relaxation allows column weights between zero and one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}\lambda_p\le1\) for every \(i\in I\).

notation.meaning: incidence of row i in column p

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Partitioning Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-cover master formulation and its linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite row set, \(P\) a finite column family, \(a_{ip}\in\{0,1\}\), and \(c_p\in\mathbb R\). The set-partitioning master is \[\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P}c_p\lambda_p:\sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}\lambda_p=1\ \text{for every }i\in I,\ \lambda_p\in\{0,1\}\ \text{for every }p\in P\right\}.\] Its linear relaxation replaces the binary restrictions by \(0\le\lambda_p\le1\) for every \(p\in P\). Every feasible integral solution covers each row with exactly one selected column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-partitioning master chooses minimum-cost columns so that every incidence row occurs in exactly one selected column; its LP relaxation allows weights between zero and one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}\lambda_p=1\) for every \(i\in I\).

notation.meaning: incidence of row i in column p

children.title: Convexified Master Representations
children.top_down_role: Master representations strengthened through convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexified Master Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-combination representation of a finite column family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be finite, let \(X=\{x^p:p\in P\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), and let \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(X)\). Membership \(x\in Q\) is represented by \[x=\sum_{p\in P}x^p\lambda_p,\qquad \sum_{p\in P}\lambda_p=1,\qquad \lambda_p\ge0\ \text{for every }p\in P.\] For any positive integer \(m\), matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), vector \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and vector \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), optimizing \(c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\) and \(x\in Q\) is equivalent to optimizing \(\sum_{p\in P}(c^\top x^p)\lambda_p\) subject to \(\sum_{p\in P}(Ax^p)\lambda_p\ge b\) and the displayed convexity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point in a finite convex hull is represented by nonnegative column weights summing to one, turning compatible linear constraints and objectives into column coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in Q\iff \exists\lambda\ge0:\ x=\sum_{p\in P}x^p\lambda_p,\ \sum_{p\in P}\lambda_p=1\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of the column points

children.title: Extended Master Representations
children.top_down_role: Master representations using auxiliary variables or expanded spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Master Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted formulation whose projection recovers the original feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). An extended master representation of \(Q\) is a system \[E=\{(x,\lambda)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^k:B x+D\lambda\le d\}\] such that its projection onto the original variables equals \(Q\): \[\operatorname{proj}_x(E)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists\lambda\in\mathbb R^k,\ Bx+D\lambda\le d\}=Q.\] The auxiliary variables \(\lambda\) may encode columns, patterns, or convex-combination weights. Optimizing an objective depending only on \(x\) over \(E\) therefore has the same feasible objective values and optimum as optimizing it over \(Q\), whenever an optimum exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended master adds auxiliary variables and constraints but projects exactly onto the original feasible region, preserving objectives that depend only on original variables.
assumptions_latex: \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+k}\) is described by linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(E)=Q\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the extended-formulation definition or projection claim.

children.title: Master-Representation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Projection and equivalence relations between the representation families.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Representation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection correspondence between convexified column weights and the original convex-hull formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be finite, let \(X=\{x^p:p\in P\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), and define \[E=\left\{(x,\lambda)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{P}:x=\sum_{p\in P}x^p\lambda_p,\ \sum_{p\in P}\lambda_p=1,\ \lambda_p\ge0\ \text{for every }p\in P\right\}.\] Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(E)=\operatorname{conv}(X)\). Hence every feasible master weight vector maps to a convexified point, and every point of the convex hull has a feasible master lift. For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), imposing \(Ax\ge b\) is equivalent under the displayed equation to imposing \(\sum_{p\in P}Ax^p\lambda_p\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex-combination master weights project exactly onto the convex hull of their columns, and compatible linear linking constraints are preserved by substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(E)=\operatorname{conv}(X)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-column LP solved within a column-generation iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a column family, let \(P'\subseteq P\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(a_p\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c_p\in\mathbb R\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Solve the restricted master \[z(P')=\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P'}c_p\lambda_p:\sum_{p\in P'}a_p\lambda_p=b,\ \lambda_p\ge0\ \text{for every }p\in P'\right\}.\] Return an optimal primal solution \(\lambda^*\) and an optimal dual vector \(\pi^*\) for \[\max\left\{b^\top\pi:a_p^\top\pi\le c_p\ \text{for every }p\in P'\right\}.\] If exact pricing over \(P\) finds a column outside \(P'\) with negative reduced cost, add one or more such columns and resolve. Stop with a full-master optimality claim only if exact pricing certifies nonnegative reduced cost for every column in \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the LP over active columns, obtain primal and dual optima, add negatively priced omitted columns, and claim full-master optimality only after exact pricing rules out every negative-reduced-cost column.
assumptions_latex: The restricted primal and dual attain finite optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\lambda^*,\pi^*)\) is an optimal primal-dual pair for the active columns \(P'\).

notation.meaning: dual vector for the master equalities

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pricing oracle for a minimization master with equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the full admissible column family, let \(a_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(c_p\in\mathbb R\) for every \(p\in P\), and let \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\) be a restricted-master dual vector. Define \(\bar c_p=c_p-a_p^\top\pi\). Assume the pricing minimum is attained, and compute \[p^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in P}\{c_p-a_p^\top\pi\}.\] If \(\bar c_{p^*}<0\), return \(p^*\) as an improving column for the minimization restricted master. If \(\bar c_{p^*}\ge0\), certify that every admissible column has nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact pricing minimizes reduced cost over all admissible columns; a negative minimum supplies an improving column, while a nonnegative minimum rules out such columns.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the full admissible column family.
The minimum reduced cost over \(P\) is attained and computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_{p^*}<0\) yields an improving column; \(\bar c_{p^*}\ge0\) implies \(\bar c_p\ge0\) for every \(p\in P\).

notation.meaning: master coefficient vector of column p

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact column-generation termination certificate for a minimization LP master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the full master \(\min\{\sum_{p\in P}c_p\lambda_p:\sum_{p\in P}a_p\lambda_p=b,\ \lambda\ge0\}\). Let \(P'\subseteq P\), and let \((\lambda^*,\pi^*)\) be an optimal primal-dual pair for its restricted master. If an exact pricing oracle certifies \[\min_{p\in P}\{c_p-a_p^\top\pi^*\}\ge0,\] then \(a_p^\top\pi^*\le c_p\) for every full-master column. Thus \(\pi^*\) is full-dual feasible, the zero extension of \(\lambda^*\) is full-primal feasible, and equality of their restricted objective values certifies full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted primal-dual optimality plus an exact certificate that every full column has nonnegative reduced cost certifies optimality for the complete LP master.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an optimal primal-dual pair \((\lambda^*,\pi^*)\).
Pricing minimizes reduced cost over the entire column family \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^*\), extended by zeros, is optimal for the full master.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically precise and its content kind matches the leaf, but no citation with an inspectable locator supports the column-generation optimality claim.

children.title: Path Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing subproblems whose columns correspond to paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Path Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained source-to-sink path pricing reduced to a shortest-path problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), arc costs \(d_e\), and a column cost constant \(\kappa\). For each admissible \(s\)-to-\(t\) path \(P\), suppose its reduced cost is \(\bar c(P)=\kappa+\sum_{e\in P}d_e\). Compute a minimum-cost \(s\)-to-\(t\) path \(P^*\). If \(\kappa+\sum_{e\in P^*}d_e<0\), return its incidence vector as an improving master column; otherwise certify that no admissible path column has negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When path reduced cost is additive over arcs, pricing is a shortest-path computation; a negative shortest-path value yields an improving column.
assumptions_latex: The admissible columns are \(s\)-to-\(t\) paths in \(G\).
Path reduced cost is additive over arcs plus \(\kappa\).
A finite minimum-cost admissible path exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{P}\bar c(P)\), and \(\bar c(P^*)\ge0\) excludes negative-reduced-cost path columns.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Shortest Path Problems p. 51
