children.title: Resource-Constrained Path Pricing
children.top_down_role: Path pricing subject to resource-feasibility restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Constrained Path Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact path pricing with additive resource bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), reduced arc costs \(d_e\in\mathbb R\), resource consumptions \(r_e\in\mathbb R_+^q\), bounds \(R\in\mathbb R_+^q\), and constant \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\). Solve exactly \[\min_{P}\left\{\kappa+\sum_{e\in P}d_e:P\text{ is an }s\text{-to-}t\text{ path},\ \sum_{e\in P}r_e\le R\right\}.\] A label-setting or label-correcting implementation may store the current vertex, accumulated resources, and accumulated cost. At the same vertex, a label may be discarded when another label uses no more of any resource and has no greater cost, with at least one strict inequality. If the exact search returns a negative optimum, return an attaining path as an improving column; if the exact optimum is nonnegative, certify that no resource-feasible path column has negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact resource-constrained path pricing minimizes reduced path cost under additive resource limits, commonly using valid dominance pruning among labels at the same vertex.
assumptions_latex: Path feasibility is determined by \(\sum_{e\in P}r_e\le R\).
The pricing search is exact and complete when used for optimality certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exact returned path minimizes reduced cost among all resource-feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) paths.

children.title: Resource-State Pricing Regimes
children.top_down_role: State-space organization induced by pricing resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-State Pricing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-expanded representation for additive-resource path pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each partial path to vertex \(v\) has an accumulated resource state \(\rho\in\mathcal R\), and traversing arc \(e=(v,w)\) applies a transition \(T_e(\rho)\). Construct a state-expanded graph with nodes \((v,\rho)\) and arcs \[(v,\rho)\longrightarrow(w,T_e(\rho))\] whenever the transition is feasible. Assign this arc the pricing cost \(d_e\). Feasible source-to-sink paths in the expanded graph correspond to feasible original paths together with their resource trajectories. If \(\mathcal R\) is finite and the correspondence preserves costs, exact pricing reduces to shortest path on the expanded graph; otherwise labels implicitly generate reachable states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource states can be made explicit as expanded graph nodes, converting feasible resource trajectories into paths and finite-state exact pricing into shortest path.
assumptions_latex: Resource evolution is determined by transitions \(T_e\).
Expanded transitions are admitted exactly when resource feasibility is preserved.
Expanded and original path costs agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible expanded paths and resource-feasible original paths correspond cost-preservingly.

notation.meaning: resource transition induced by arc e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state-expanded representation fits the leaf and is internally coherent under its exact-transition assumptions, but no inspectable source supports the correspondence or finite-state shortest-path reduction.

children.title: Knapsack Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing interfaces governed by knapsack structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary capacity-feasible column pricing with additive reduced profit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let items \(j\in J\) have weights \(w_j\ge0\), capacity \(W\ge0\), and reduced-profit coefficients \(q_j\). Solve the binary knapsack problem \[x^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}\left\{\sum_{j\in J}q_jx_j:\sum_{j\in J}w_jx_j\le W,\ x_j\in\{0,1\}\right\}.\] If the associated master column has reduced cost \(\bar c(x)=\kappa-\sum_{j\in J}q_jx_j\), return \(x^*\) when \(\bar c(x^*)<0\). When the knapsack optimum is exact and \(\bar c(x^*)\ge0\), certify that no capacity-feasible binary pattern has negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Knapsack pricing finds the capacity-feasible item pattern of maximum reduced profit and returns it precisely when its resulting master reduced cost is negative.
assumptions_latex: Admissible columns are exactly the capacity-feasible binary patterns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) minimizes \(\bar c(x)=\kappa-\sum_{j\in J}q_jx_j\) over all admissible patterns.

children.title: Packing Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing interfaces governed by packing feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Packing Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary packing form of a column-generation pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be a finite item set, let \(B\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m\times I}\), and let \(d\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\). Given item reduced-cost contributions \(q_i\in\mathbb{R}\) and a column offset \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), packing pricing is
\[\min\left\{\alpha+\sum_{i\in I}q_i x_i:Bx\le d,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{I}\right\}.\]
Each feasible vector encodes a permissible packed column. For a minimization master, a column is improving exactly when its objective value is negative; otherwise this pricing family certifies only that no improving packing column exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Packing pricing minimizes reduced cost over binary selections satisfying multidimensional capacity constraints; a negative optimum supplies an improving column.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and the number of capacity rows \(m\) are finite.
Reduced costs are evaluated at a fixed restricted-master dual vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) yields an improving packing column iff \(\alpha+\sum_{i\in I}q_i x_i^*<0\).

notation.meaning: indicator that item i belongs to the generated column

children.title: Capacity-Coupled Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes where shared capacities couple column components.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Coupled Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing with several decisions coupled through shared capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) index component decisions, with local feasible sets \(X_k\), resource matrices \(B_k\), and shared capacity \(d\). Given local reduced-cost functions \(r_k:X_k\to\mathbb{R}\) and offset \(\alpha\), capacity-coupled pricing is
\[\min\left\{\alpha+\sum_{k\in K}r_k(x^k):x^k\in X_k\ \forall k,\ \sum_{k\in K}B_kx^k\le d\right\}.\]
The shared inequality prevents independent solution of the component pricing problems in general. For a minimization master, any feasible tuple with negative objective defines an improving composite column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capacity-coupled pricing joins local pricing decisions through shared resource limits and returns an improving composite column when the minimum reduced cost is negative.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite and each \(X_k\) is nonempty.
All vectors \(B_kx^k\) have the dimension of \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible tuple \((x^k)_{k\in K}\) is improving whenever \(\alpha+\sum_{k\in K}r_k(x^k)<0\).

notation.meaning: local feasible set for component k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separable reduced costs with a shared packing constraint define capacity-coupled pricing

children.title: Assignment Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing subproblems based on assignment structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bipartite one-to-one assignment form of reduced-cost pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) and \(V\) be finite sets and \(E\subseteq U\times V\) the admissible assignments. Given reduced-cost coefficients \(q_{uv}\) and offset \(\alpha\), assignment pricing solves
\[\min\left\{\alpha+\sum_{(u,v)\in E}q_{uv}x_{uv}:\sum_{v:(u,v)\in E}x_{uv}\le1\ \forall u,\ \sum_{u:(u,v)\in E}x_{uv}\le1\ \forall v,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{E}\right\}.\]
Required assignments may replace selected inequalities by equalities. A negative optimum generates an improving assignment column for a minimization master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assignment pricing finds a minimum-reduced-cost matching in an admissible bipartite graph; a negative optimum identifies an improving assignment column.
assumptions_latex: The coefficients \(q_{uv}\) include the current master-dual contributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal matching \(x^*\) produces an improving column iff \(\alpha+\sum_{(u,v)\in E}q_{uv}x_{uv}^*<0\).

notation.meaning: admissible edges of the bipartite assignment graph

children.title: Scheduling Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing subproblems based on scheduling structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost optimization over complete feasible schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\) be a finite job set and let \(\mathcal{S}\) be the family of schedules satisfying the local machine, precedence, release-time, and compatibility restrictions of one generated column. For each \(S\in\mathcal{S}\), let \(c(S)\) be its original cost and \(a(S)\) its master-incidence vector. At master dual vector \(\pi\), scheduling pricing solves
\[\min_{S\in\mathcal{S}}\bar c(S),\qquad \bar c(S)=c(S)-\pi^{\mathsf T}a(S).\]
For a minimization master, a schedule with \(\bar c(S)<0\) is an improving column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scheduling pricing minimizes reduced cost over locally feasible schedules, returning a schedule column when its reduced cost is negative.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{S}\) precisely represents the schedules allowed for one master column.
\(\pi\) is dual-feasible for the current restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(S^*\in\arg\min_{S\in\mathcal{S}}\bar c(S)\), then \(S^*\) is improving iff \(\bar c(S^*)<0\).

children.title: Time-Indexed Pricing Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Indexed Pricing Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-indexed representation of a scheduling pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) be a finite set of time indices and let \(x_{jt}=1\) mean that job \(j\) starts at time \(t\). A time-indexed pricing interface represents its feasible columns by \(x\in X_T\), where \(X_T\) enforces admissible starts, job-selection rules, and all resource constraints at every time. Given coefficients \(q_{jt}\) and offset \(\alpha\), the oracle returns
\[\min\left\{\alpha+\sum_{j}\sum_{t\in T}q_{jt}x_{jt}:x\in X_T\right\}\]
and the selected job-time incidences required to construct the master column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-indexed interface exposes scheduling columns through binary job-start variables, timewise feasibility constraints, and a dual-adjusted objective.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is finite and contains every admissible start time.
\(X_T\) encodes all local scheduling restrictions needed by the master column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any optimizer \(x^*\) with \(\alpha+\sum_j\sum_{t\in T}q_{jt}x_{jt}^*<0\) represents an improving time-indexed column.

notation.meaning: indicator that job j starts at time t

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of restricted-master dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be the restricted-master dual feasible set, \(\theta:D\to\mathbb{R}\) its concave objective, \(\bar\pi\) a stability center, and \(\rho>0\). At an iteration, compute
\[\pi^+\in\arg\max_{\pi\in D}\left\{\theta(\pi)-\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert\pi-\bar\pi\rVert_2^2\right\},\]
price columns using \(\pi^+\), and add any improving columns. After a prescribed serious-step test, set \(\bar\pi\leftarrow\pi^+\); otherwise retain the center and adjust \(\rho\). Stop only when exact pricing finds no improving column, and output the current master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal dual stabilization penalizes movement from a stability center, updates that center after serious progress, and retains exact pricing for termination.
assumptions_latex: Exact pricing is invoked before declaring termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is valid only when exact pricing at the final dual vector returns no negative-reduced-cost column.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal regularization is a standard dual-stabilization mechanism in column generation

children.title: Partial Pricing

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic pricing over a proper subset of pricing blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the complete column family as \(\mathcal{C}=\bigcup_{k=1}^K\mathcal{C}_k\). Initialize an active block set \(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}\). At each restricted-master dual vector \(\pi\), solve pricing only over \(\bigcup_{k\in A}\mathcal{C}_k\); add any negative-reduced-cost columns and update \(A\) by a prescribed cyclic or adaptive rule. If active blocks yield none, inspect all omitted blocks before stopping. Output the restricted-master solution only after every block has certified nonnegative minimum reduced cost at the same final dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial pricing searches selected column blocks first but must price every omitted block before certifying global column-generation termination.
assumptions_latex: The blocks cover the entire column family \(\mathcal{C}\).
Each block can be priced exactly for the final termination test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global termination requires \(\min_{c\in\mathcal{C}_k}\bar c_c(\pi)\ge0\) for every \(k=1,\ldots,K\).

children.title: Multiple-Column Pricing

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Column Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generation of several improving columns per pricing call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a restricted-master dual vector \(\pi\), a feasible column family \(\mathcal{C}\), and a batch limit \(L\ge1\), compute a set \(B\subseteq\mathcal{C}\) of distinct columns satisfying \(|B|\le L\) and \(\bar c_c(\pi)<0\) for every \(c\in B\). Prefer the \(L\) smallest reduced costs when that enumeration is available. Add \(B\) simultaneously and reoptimize the restricted master. If no column is returned, run an exact minimum-reduced-cost pricing oracle; stop only if its optimum is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple-column pricing adds a batch of distinct improving columns per iteration, while an exact oracle remains necessary for a valid stopping certificate.
assumptions_latex: Reduced costs are computed at one fixed dual vector \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned column is improving, and termination is certified only if \(\min_{c\in\mathcal{C}}\bar c_c(\pi)\ge0\).

children.title: Heuristic Pricing
children.top_down_role: Approximate search used to identify improving columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact search for improving columns with exact fallback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a dual vector \(\pi\), apply a heuristic map \(H\) to produce a finite candidate set \(H(\pi)\subseteq\mathcal{C}\). Evaluate every candidate's true reduced cost and add any \(c\) satisfying \(\bar c_c(\pi)<0\). If the heuristic returns no improving column, either continue without an optimality claim or invoke an exact oracle computing \(\min_{c\in\mathcal{C}}\bar c_c(\pi)\). Stop column generation only when that exact minimum is nonnegative; heuristic failure alone is not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heuristic pricing searches cheaply for improving columns, but only exact pricing can certify that no negative-reduced-cost column remains.
assumptions_latex: Every heuristic candidate belongs to the valid column family \(\mathcal{C}\).
Candidate reduced costs are evaluated exactly before insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(\pi)\cap\{c:\bar c_c(\pi)<0\}=\varnothing\) does not imply \(\min_{c\in\mathcal{C}}\bar c_c(\pi)\ge0\).

children.title: Restricted-Master Initialization
children.top_down_role: Construction of a viable initial restricted master.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase-I construction of an initially feasible restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an initial finite column set \(\mathcal{C}_0\). If its restricted master may be infeasible, introduce nonnegative artificial variables \(s\) so that every master row can be satisfied, and solve the phase-I problem
\[\min\{\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}s:A_{\mathcal{C}_0}\lambda+Rs=b,\ \lambda\ge0,\ s\ge0\},\]
where \(R\) supplies appropriate signed unit columns. Use phase-I dual prices to generate genuine columns. Continue until the artificial objective is zero, then remove artificial variables and optimize the original restricted master. A positive phase-I optimum after exhaustive exact pricing certifies infeasibility of the full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-master initialization uses genuine seed columns and phase-I artificial variables, then prices genuine columns until all artificial mass vanishes or infeasibility is certified.
assumptions_latex: The artificial-column matrix \(R\) makes the phase-I restricted master feasible.
Pricing is exact before declaring full-master infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Original restricted-master feasibility is obtained when the phase-I optimum equals \(0\); a positive exhaustive phase-I optimum certifies full-master infeasibility.

children.title: Column Pool Management
children.top_down_role: Organization and reuse of generated columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Pool Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintenance and reuse of generated columns outside the active basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an active restricted-master set \(A\) and a finite pool \(P\) of valid previously generated columns. At dual vector \(\pi\), recompute \(\bar c_c(\pi)\) for eligible \(c\in P\setminus A\), move selected negative-reduced-cost columns into \(A\), and insert newly priced valid columns into both sets. Apply deterministic capacity, duplication, and retention rules to \(P\). If the pool contains no improving column, call the complete pricing oracle; pool exhaustion alone must not terminate column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column pool management stores, re-evaluates, activates, deduplicates, and retires valid columns, without replacing exact pricing in the stopping test.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(P\) is a valid full-master column.
Reduced costs are recomputed whenever the dual vector changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only complete pricing, not \(\min_{c\in P}\bar c_c(\pi)\ge0\), can certify absence of improving full-master columns.

notation.meaning: current reduced cost of stored column c

children.title: Column Aging Policies

knowledge_statements.title: Column Aging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-based inactivity counters for column retention decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assign each managed column \(c\) an age \(a_c^0=0\) and choose a threshold \(L\ge1\). After restricted-master iteration \(t\), set
\[a_c^{t+1}=\begin{cases}0,&\lambda_c^t>\varepsilon\ \text{or }c\text{ is basic},\\a_c^t+1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\]
for a fixed tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Mark \(c\) as stale when \(a_c^{t+1}\ge L\). Staleness may trigger transfer to a pool or deletion, but it does not establish that the column can never again have negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column’s age counts consecutive inactive iterations; reaching a threshold permits retirement but gives no permanent reduced-cost certificate.
assumptions_latex: Activity is assessed consistently using \(\varepsilon\) and basis status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_c^{t+1}\ge L\) certifies only policy-defined staleness, not future nonimprovement of column \(c\).

notation.meaning: age of column c after iteration t
restricted-master value of column c at iteration t

children.title: Column Deletion Policies
children.top_down_role: Removal regimes for inactive or redundant columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Deletion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe lifecycle rule for a minimization restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a restricted-master column set \(P_t\), incumbent basic set \(B_t\subseteq P_t\), reduced costs \(\bar c_p^t\), and ages \(a_p^t\), choose thresholds \(A\in\mathbb N\) and \(\delta\geq0\). Form \(D_t=\{p\in P_t\setminus B_t:a_p^t\geq A,\ \bar c_p^t\geq-\delta\}\), retain \(P_{t+1}=P_t\setminus D_t\), and archive every deleted column with its coefficients and cost. Reset \(a_p^{t+1}=0\) when \(p\) is basic or has \(\bar c_p^t< -\delta\); otherwise set \(a_p^{t+1}=a_p^t+1\). Because the pricing oracle still ranges over the full column universe, any deleted improving column may be regenerated. Stop only after exact pricing certifies that no admissible column has negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only old, nonbasic, nonimproving columns, retain reconstructible data, and keep pricing over the full column universe so deleted improving columns can return.
assumptions_latex: Reduced costs and exact pricing use the current restricted-master dual solution.
Deleted columns remain representable by the pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{t+1}=P_t\setminus D_t\), while exact pricing preserves the restricted-master optimality test over the full column universe.

notation.meaning: active restricted-master columns at iteration t
columns basic in the current master solution

children.title: Nodewise Column Generation

knowledge_statements.title: Nodewise Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-bound computation at one branch-and-price node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search node \(v\), let \(X_v\) denote the columns satisfying all branching decisions inherited by \(v\). Initialize a feasible restricted set \(P_v\subseteq X_v\). Repeatedly solve the restricted master over \(P_v\), obtain dual multipliers \(\pi_v\), and solve exact pricing \(p^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in X_v}\{c_p-\pi_v^{\mathsf T}a_p\}\). If its reduced cost is negative, add \(p^*\) to \(P_v\) and repeat. Otherwise the restricted-master value equals the optimum of the node LP over \(X_v\). Output that value and solution as the node bound; fathom, accept an integral solution, or branch according to the global search rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each search node, generate only branch-feasible columns until exact pricing finds none improving; the resulting master value is the node LP bound.
assumptions_latex: The node restricted master is feasible or feasibility pricing is available.
Pricing optimizes over every column satisfying the node's branching restrictions.
The restricted master and pricing problem are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the minimum nodewise reduced cost is nonnegative, the restricted-master optimum is the full node-LP optimum.

notation.meaning: columns admissible at search node v
active restricted-master columns at node v

children.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching structures that preserve tractable pricing interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for branch decisions in column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_v\) be the column family at node \(v\), and let a branch create children \(w\) by imposing predicates \(g_w(p)\in\{0,1\}\) on individual columns. The branch is pricing-compatible if: the child families \(X_w=\{p\in X_v:g_w(p)=1\}\) cover every integer solution feasible at \(v\); their corresponding integer-solution regions are mutually disjoint; and, for every dual vector \(\pi\), the optimization \(\min_{p\in X_w}\{c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p\}\) remains exactly solvable by the designated pricing method, possibly after modifying its state space or resources. Thus branching partitions integer solutions without destroying the ability to certify child LP bounds by pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch is pricing-compatible when its children partition the node’s integer solutions and exact reduced-cost pricing remains solvable under every child restriction.
assumptions_latex: Each master column \(p\) has coefficient vector \(a_p\) and cost \(c_p\).
Branching restrictions can be expressed as predicates on columns or pricing states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each child admits exact pricing, and the children form a valid exhaustive disjunction for the parent integer solutions.

notation.meaning: column family admissible at parent node v

children.title: Tree-Level Bound Management
children.top_down_role: Coordination of restricted-master bounds across the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Level Bound Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower-bound and incumbent handling for minimization branch-and-price.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each live node \(v\), maintain a certified LP lower bound \(L_v\) obtained after exact nodewise pricing, and maintain incumbent integer value \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Update \(U\) whenever a better feasible integer solution is found. Fathom node \(v\) if it is infeasible, its priced LP solution is integral, or \(L_v\geq U-\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\geq0\) is the prescribed absolute tolerance. Define the global lower bound by \(L=\min_{v\in\mathcal O}L_v\) over open nodes \(\mathcal O\); if \(\mathcal O=\varnothing\), set \(L=U\). Terminate when \(\mathcal O=\varnothing\) or \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\), returning the incumbent and the certified gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track certified node lower bounds and the best integer incumbent; prune dominated nodes and stop when no nodes remain or the global gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization integer program.
Every stored node bound follows exact pricing or another valid lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(L\leq z^*\leq U\) and either the tree is exhausted or \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at node v
value of the best known feasible integer solution

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract representation of branching families that preserve pricing structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing-compatible branching family is represented by a collection \(\mathcal G\) of finite disjunctions \(G=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)\). For every admissible parent column family \(X\), the induced child families are \(X_i=\{p\in X:g_i(p)=1\}\). The representation is valid when the associated child integer-feasible regions partition the parent integer-feasible region and each reduced-cost problem \(\min_{p\in X_i}\{c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p\}\) belongs to the same exactly solvable pricing class for every dual vector \(\pi\). Typical realizations encode \(g_i\) by forbidding or requiring an item pair, arc, edge, resource transition, or other feature already expressible in the pricing state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Such a family consists of exhaustive branching disjunctions whose child restrictions can be embedded in the existing exact pricing problem.
assumptions_latex: The parent master uses a well-defined column family \(X\).
Integer solutions are finite combinations of columns from \(X\).
The pricing class is specified before compatibility is assessed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(G\in\mathcal G\) yields an exhaustive integer disjunction whose child reduced-cost problems remain exactly solvable in the designated pricing class.

notation.meaning: column family admitted by child i

children.title: Cut-Enhanced Restricted Masters
children.top_down_role: Restricted masters strengthened by valid inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Enhanced Restricted Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted master augmented by valid inequalities with column-dependent coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P'\subseteq P\) be the active columns of a minimization master, with variables \(\lambda_p\geq0\). A cut-enhanced restricted master has the form \[\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P'}c_p\lambda_p:\ \sum_{p\in P'}a_p\lambda_p\geq b,\ \sum_{p\in P'}d_{kp}\lambda_p\geq e_k\ \text{for all }k\in K',\ \lambda_p\geq0\right\}.\] Each added inequality must be valid for the intended full-master feasible region, and its coefficient \(d_{kp}\) must be computable for every generated column. If \(\pi\) and \(\mu\) are dual multipliers for the original rows and cuts, respectively, then column \(p\) has reduced cost \(\bar c_p=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\sum_{k\in K'}\mu_kd_{kp}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut-enhanced restricted master adds valid inequalities whose coefficients are computable for every column and whose dual multipliers modify reduced-cost pricing.
assumptions_latex: \(P'\) and the active cut set \(K'\) are finite.
Every active cut is valid for the full-master feasible region.
The sign convention matches the displayed covering-form master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented master is a valid restricted relaxation, with reduced costs \(\bar c_p=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\sum_{k\in K'}\mu_kd_{kp}\).

children.title: Pricing under Added Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing under Added Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost pricing after cut duals enter the column objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given original-row duals \(\pi\), active-cut duals \(\mu_k\), column cost \(c_p\), original coefficients \(a_p\), and cut coefficients \(d_{kp}\), solve \[p^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in P}\left(c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\sum_{k\in K'}\mu_kd_{kp}\right).\] If the attained reduced cost is negative, compute all coefficients of \(p^*\), add that column to the restricted master, and reoptimize. Otherwise stop pricing and certify optimality of the current cut-enhanced master over the full column family. This procedure is exact only when every active cut coefficient can be evaluated within the pricing oracle and the displayed minimization is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorporate every active cut’s dual-weighted column coefficient into reduced cost, add a negative-cost minimizer, and certify completion only after exact global pricing.
assumptions_latex: The full column family \(P\) is the pricing domain.
All active-cut coefficients \(d_{kp}\) are computable during pricing.
The pricing minimization is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonnegative minimum reduced cost certifies optimality of the current cut-enhanced master over all columns in \(P\).

children.title: Global Cut Coordination
children.top_down_role: Management of globally valid cuts throughout branch-price search.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and synchronization rules for cuts across a branch-price tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a global cut pool \(K_G\) containing only inequalities valid for the root integer-feasible region, and local pools \(K_v\) containing inequalities valid under node \(v\)'s inherited restrictions. When processing \(v\), activate selected cuts from \(K_G\cup K_u\), where \(u\) ranges over ancestors of \(v\), but never propagate a merely local cut outside its descendant subtree. For every activated cut, install both its restricted-master row and its coefficient evaluator in pricing before using its dual multiplier. If a global cut is added, invalidate or recompute affected node bounds not derived with an equivalent relaxation. Node pruning may use only bounds certified for the node's current active global and inherited local cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate globally valid and subtree-local cuts, synchronize each active cut with pricing, and use only bounds certified for the current cut system.
assumptions_latex: The search tree has a fixed ancestor relation.
Each cut carries a verified validity scope.
Node bounds are tagged with the cut system used to compute them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No cut is applied outside its validity scope, and every pruning bound corresponds to a pricing-synchronized node relaxation.

notation.meaning: cuts local to node v and its descendants

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Primal Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of a full integer solution from generated columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P'\subseteq P\) be the generated columns after solving a restricted-master relaxation. Form the restricted integer master by imposing the original integrality requirements on \(\lambda_p\) for \(p\in P'\), together with all original linking constraints. Solve this finite integer program to obtain \(\hat\lambda\). If it is feasible, extend it to the full master by setting \(\hat\lambda_p=0\) for \(p\in P\setminus P'\); the extension is a valid full-master integer solution and supplies an incumbent. If the restricted integer master is infeasible, enlarge \(P'\) by heuristic or exact column generation and repeat. Recovery certifies feasibility, but not global integer optimality unless the remaining search establishes a matching bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the integer master over generated columns; zero-extension yields a valid incumbent when feasible, but optimality still requires a matching global bound.
assumptions_latex: Every generated column is admissible for the full master.
The restricted integer master retains all original linking constraints.
Omitted column variables may validly be fixed to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any feasible restricted integer solution extends by zeros to a feasible full-master integer solution of the same objective value.

children.title: Restricted-Master Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degenerate restricted-master behavior affecting column-generation progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy condition for a standard-form restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the restricted master \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\). A basic feasible solution associated with basis \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(|B|=m\), is degenerate precisely when \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\geq0\) and at least one basic component satisfies \((x_B)_i=0\). Equivalently, fewer than \(m\) components of that basic feasible solution are strictly positive. Degeneracy permits a simplex pivot or addition of a negative-reduced-cost column to change the basis without changing the primal point or objective value, although such stalling is possible rather than necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-master basic solution is degenerate when at least one basic variable is zero; basis changes can then occur without primal or objective progress.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is in equality standard form.
\(B\) is a nonsingular basis yielding a feasible basic solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy holds if and only if \(\min_{i\in B}(x_B)_i=0\), and it makes zero-step basis changes possible.

notation.meaning: index set of a restricted-master basis

children.title: Column-Generation Tailing-Off
children.top_down_role: Late-stage progress deterioration in column-generation runs.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Tailing-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational pathology of vanishing late-stage master improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_t\) be the restricted-master objective value after iteration \(t\) of a minimization column-generation method, and let \(r_t<0\) be the reduced cost of the column added at that iteration. For tolerances \(\eta>0\) and an integer window \(q\geq1\), a tailing-off episode is detected at \(t\) when \[0\leq z_{t-q}-z_t\leq\eta\quad\text{and}\quad r_s<0\ \text{for every }s=t-q+1,\ldots,t.\] Thus pricing continues to find improving columns, yet the accumulated bound improvement over the window is negligible. This is a progress diagnostic, not an optimality certificate: termination still requires an exact nonnegative minimum reduced cost or another valid bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing-off occurs when several negative-reduced-cost columns produce negligible cumulative master improvement; it diagnoses slow progress but does not certify optimality.
assumptions_latex: Restricted-master values \(z_t\) are measured after reoptimization.
The problem is a minimization problem.
The thresholds \(\eta\) and \(q\) are fixed diagnostic parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed window condition diagnoses tailing-off but cannot replace the exact reduced-cost stopping test.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of the column added at iteration t

children.title: Dual Instability
children.top_down_role: Unstable dual information affecting pricing guidance.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oscillation among dual optima that destabilizes pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_t\) be the optimal-dual set of the restricted master at iteration \(t\), let the solver select \(\pi_t\in D_t\), and let \(r(p;\pi)=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p\). Dual instability is present over iterations \(s,\ldots,t\) when the master values change by at most a prescribed \(\eta\geq0\), while selected duals satisfy \(\max_{i,j\in\{s,\ldots,t\}}\|\pi_i-\pi_j\|>\Delta\) for a prescribed \(\Delta>0\), and these changes alter the identity or ranking of negative-reduced-cost columns. Multiple or nearly multiple dual optima commonly permit this behavior. The condition diagnoses unstable pricing signals; it neither implies primal infeasibility nor invalidates an exact reduced-cost optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual instability means nearly unchanged master values accompany large dual movements that materially change which columns pricing regards as attractive.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\pi_t\) is dual-optimal for its iteration's restricted master.
A norm and diagnostic thresholds \(\eta,\Delta\) are fixed.
Column reduced costs use a consistent sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large dual variation with negligible value change and altered pricing rankings constitutes instability, but does not invalidate exact pricing certificates.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of column p under dual vector pi

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for exact reduced-cost minimization over an implicitly represented column family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dual vector \(\pi\), exact pricing computes \(z_{\mathrm{price}}(\pi)=\min_{c\in\mathcal C}\bar c_{\pi}(c)\), or decides whether \(z_{\mathrm{price}}(\pi)<0\). If this decision problem is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions, then a polynomial-time exact pricing oracle for all encoded instances would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\). Consequently, column generation does not by itself yield a polynomial-time solution method when its pricing subproblem is computationally hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If detecting a negative-reduced-cost column is NP-hard, exact polynomial-time pricing, and hence a general polynomial-time column-generation implementation, is unavailable unless P equals NP.
knowledge_statements.title: Computationally Hard Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity implication is mathematically plausible and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but the record has no citation supporting the NP-hard pricing premise or the stated consequence for exact column generation. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-error boundary for minimization pricing in linear column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an inexact pricing oracle returns a column with value \(\widehat z\) satisfying \(z_{\mathrm{price}}\le \widehat z\le z_{\mathrm{price}}+\varepsilon\), where \(z_{\mathrm{price}}=\min_{c\in\mathcal C}\bar c(c)\). If the algorithm stops when \(\widehat z\ge 0\), it can stop while \(-\varepsilon\le z_{\mathrm{price}}<0\). Thus an improving column may remain, and exact master-LP optimality follows only when \(\varepsilon=0\), or when an independent valid lower bound proves \(z_{\mathrm{price}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive-error pricing oracle may miss columns with reduced cost between minus epsilon and zero, so its stopping test certifies only approximate, not exact, master optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error inequalities and resulting interval for an undetected improving column are internally consistent, and failure_boundary is the correct role. No source with a specific locator is cited for this inexact-pricing stopping boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes heuristic pricing termination from a verifiable full-master optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing certificate at dual vector \(\pi\) is a verifiable bound \(L\) satisfying \(L\le\min_{c\in\mathcal C}\bar c_{\pi}(c)\). If \(L\ge0\), every full-master column has nonnegative reduced cost, so \(\pi\) is feasible for the full dual and the optimal restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master. Merely failing to find a negative-reduced-cost column supplies no such bound; the gap between search failure and a certified \(L\ge0\) is the pricing-certificate gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to find an improving column is not a certificate; full-master optimality requires a verifiable global lower bound showing that every reduced cost is nonnegative.

children.title: Column-Space Symmetry
children.top_down_role: Symmetric column families that produce equivalent representations.

assumptions_latex: The group action preserves the master formulation data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Columns in one orbit are interchangeable in the master and have equal reduced cost for every dual vector.

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symmetry of master columns, not merely equality at one dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a master formulation have columns \(a_j\) and costs \(c_j\) indexed by \(j\in J\). A column-space symmetry is an action of a group \(G\) on \(J\) such that \(a_{g j}=a_j\) and \(c_{g j}=c_j\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(j\in J\). Hence each orbit \(G j\) consists of interchangeable columns and, for every dual vector \(\pi\), satisfies \(c_{g j}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{g j}=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column-space symmetry permutes column indices while preserving each column's master coefficients and cost, making all members of an orbit interchangeable and equally priced.
knowledge_statements.title: Column-Space Symmetry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed condition consistently defines an exact data-preserving action, but it is narrower than many formulation-symmetry notions because it requires each indexed column and cost to remain identical rather than permitting coordinated row or model transformations. A source is needed to establish that this is the intended local meaning of Column-Space Symmetry.

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathology caused by repeatedly inserting master-identical columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generated column \(k\) duplicates an existing column \(j\) when \(a_k=a_j\), \(c_k=c_j\), and both variables have the same bounds and integrality status. Replacing \((x_j,x_k)\) by \(x'_j=x_j+x_k\) preserves the master constraints and objective whenever their bounds permit this aggregation. Therefore insertion of \(k\) does not improve the represented feasible set or optimal value, but repeated insertion can increase restricted-master size, degeneracy, and cycling risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generating a column identical in coefficients, cost, bounds, and type to an existing one adds no represented solution but can worsen size and degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Column Generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but the mathematical claim is false under the stated hypotheses. Adding a second identical bounded or binary variable can enlarge the attainable aggregate range and can change the feasible set or optimum; identical bounds and integrality status do not prevent this. The claim would require an appropriate continuous unbounded-variable setting or explicit aggregate-bound and multiplicity semantics.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplicate suppression under a specified column-equivalence relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a generated column \(c\), an equivalence relation \(\sim\), a canonicalization map satisfying \(c\sim d\) if and only if \(\kappa(c)=\kappa(d)\), and the key set \(H\) of restricted-master columns. Compute \(h=\kappa(c)\). If \(h\in H\), discard \(c\); otherwise insert the chosen representative of \([c]_{\sim}\) and update \(H\leftarrow H\cup\{h\}\). Repeat after each pricing call and terminate according to the underlying column-generation stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map every generated column to an exact canonical key, discard it when that key is present, and otherwise insert one representative and record its key.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Given the stated exact biconditional for the canonical key, the procedure inserts at most one equivalence-class representative, and algorithm is the correct content kind. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncapacitated facility location formulation and LP dual bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the uncapacitated facility location objective, its standard integer and linear programming formulations, and the associated dual lower bound; the metric variant additionally assumes metric assignment costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For facility set $F$, client set $D$, opening costs $f_i$, and assignment costs $c_{ij}$, uncapacitated facility location minimizes $\sum_{i\in F'}f_i+\sum_{j\in D}\min_{i\in F'}c_{ij}$ over $F'\subseteq F$. Equivalently, its integer formulation is $\min \sum_i f_i y_i+\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}x_{ij}$ subject to $\sum_i x_{ij}=1$ for every $j$, $x_{ij}\le y_i$ for every $i,j$, and $x_{ij},y_i\in\{0,1\}$. Replacing integrality by $x_{ij},y_i\ge0$ gives an LP whose dual is $\max\sum_jv_j$ subject to $\sum_jw_{ij}\le f_i$, $v_j-w_{ij}\le c_{ij}$, and $w_{ij}\ge0$. Hence every dual-feasible $(v,w)$ satisfies $\sum_jv_j\le Z_{LP}^*\le\mathrm{OPT}$. In the metric variant, clients and facilities are points of a metric space, so in particular $c_{ij}\le c_{il}+c_{kl}+c_{kj}$ for all clients $j,l$ and facilities $i,k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose facilities to open and assign every client to one open facility, minimizing opening plus assignment costs. Binary opening and assignment variables yield the standard integer formulation; relaxing them to nonnegative variables gives an LP with the displayed dual. Every feasible dual objective is a lower bound on both the LP optimum and the integral optimum. In metric facility location, assignment costs arise from a metric and obey the corresponding triangle inequality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric uncapacitated facility location LP and dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem formulation, LP relaxation, dual cost-share interpretation, and dual lower bound for metric uncapacitated facility location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a set of facilities and \(D\) a set of clients, with opening costs \(f_i\) and metric assignment costs \(c_{ij}\). The relaxation is \[\min \sum_{i\in F}f_i y_i+\sum_{i\in F,j\in D}c_{ij}x_{ij}\] subject to \(\sum_{i\in F}x_{ij}=1\) for every \(j\in D\), \(x_{ij}\le y_i\), and \(x_{ij},y_i\ge0\). Its dual is \[\max \sum_{j\in D}v_j\] subject to \(\sum_{j\in D}w_{ij}\le f_i\), \(v_j-w_{ij}\le c_{ij}\), and \(w_{ij}\ge0\). Consequently, every dual-feasible \((v,w)\) supplies a lower bound on the optimal facility-location cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric uncapacitated facility location minimizes facility-opening and client-assignment costs. Its standard assignment-opening relaxation has a dual whose client values and nonnegative facility cost shares provide a lower bound on the optimal integral cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncapacitated and Metric Uncapacitated Facility Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines uncapacitated facility location and the condition termed metric service costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) and \(\mathcal F\) be finite sets of customers and potential facilities, with \(f_i\in\mathbb R_+\) and \(c_{ij}\in\mathbb R_+\). Uncapacitated facility location minimizes \(\sum_{i\in X}f_i+\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}c_{\sigma(j)j}\) over \(X\subseteq\mathcal F\) and assignments \(\sigma:\mathcal D\to X\). The costs are called metric service costs when \(c_{ij}+c_{i'j}+c_{i'j'}\ge c_{ij'}\) for all \(i,i'\in\mathcal F\) and \(j,j'\in\mathcal D\). Under this condition the cross-set costs extend to a semimetric on \(\mathcal D\cup\mathcal F\) by symmetry, zero diagonal, \(c_{ii'}:=\min_{j\in\mathcal D}(c_{ij}+c_{i'j})\) for distinct facilities, and \(c_{jj'}:=\min_{i\in\mathcal F}(c_{ij}+c_{ij'})\) for distinct customers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncapacitated facility location selects facilities and assigns every customer to an open facility to minimize opening plus service costs. The text calls the service costs metric when the stated four-point inequality holds; that condition permits their extension to a semimetric on all customers and facilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{X\subseteq\mathcal F,\,\sigma:\mathcal D\to X}\left(\sum_{i\in X}f_i+\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}c_{\sigma(j)j}\right),\qquad c_{ij}+c_{i'j}+c_{i'j'}\ge c_{ij'}\ \forall i,i'\in\mathcal F,\ j,j'\in\mathcal D\Longrightarrow\text{a semimetric extension exists}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric Uncapacitated Facility Location and Its LP Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines metric uncapacitated facility location, its standard primal–dual LP pair, and neighborhoods induced by an optimal primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given client set $D$, facility set $F$, opening costs $f_i$, and metric assignment costs $c_{ij}$, uncapacitated facility location minimizes the total opening and assignment cost. Its LP relaxation is $\min \sum_{i\in F}f_i y_i+\sum_{i\in F,j\in D}c_{ij}x_{ij}$ subject to $\sum_{i\in F}x_{ij}=1$ for every $j\in D$, $x_{ij}\le y_i$, and $x_{ij},y_i\ge0$. Its dual is $\max\sum_{j\in D}v_j$ subject to $\sum_{j\in D}w_{ij}\le f_i$, $v_j-w_{ij}\le c_{ij}$, and $w_{ij}\ge0$, with each $v_j$ unrestricted. For an optimal primal solution $(x^*,y^*)$, define $N(j)=\{i\in F:x^*_{ij}>0\}$ and $N^2(j)=\{k\in D:\exists i\in N(j)\text{ such that }x^*_{ik}>0\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric uncapacitated facility location selects facilities and assigns every client to an open facility while minimizing opening and assignment costs. Its standard LP has fractional opening and assignment variables, and its dual has unrestricted client variables and nonnegative facility-client variables. Positive optimal assignments define client neighborhoods and two-hop client neighborhoods.

f_i\text{ is the opening cost of facility }i
c_{ij}\text{ is the metric distance between facility }i\text{ and client }j
(x^*,y^*)\text{ is an optimal solution of the primal relaxation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{UFL}\text{ has the stated primal--dual LP formulation and the induced neighborhoods }N(j)\text{ and }N^2(j).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Facility-Set Representation of Metric Uncapacitated Facility Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eliminates explicit assignment variables by assigning each customer to a nearest open facility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For metric service costs and any nonempty \(X\subseteq\mathcal F\), a best assignment \(\sigma:\mathcal D\to X\) satisfies \(c_{\sigma(j)j}=\min_{i\in X}c_{ij}\) for every \(j\in\mathcal D\). Hence define \(c_F(X):=\sum_{i\in X}f_i\) and \(c_S(X):=\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}\min_{i\in X}c_{ij}\); the problem is equivalently \(\min_{\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\mathcal F}\bigl(c_F(X)+c_S(X)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any nonempty open-facility set under metric service costs, each customer can optimally be assigned to a nearest open facility. Thus an instance can be represented solely by a nonempty facility set, whose objective is its total opening cost plus the sum of nearest-facility service costs.
assumptions_latex: c\text{ is a metric service-cost system}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\sigma:\mathcal D\to X}\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}c_{\sigma(j)j}=\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}\min_{i\in X}c_{ij},\qquad \mathrm{OPT}=\min_{\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\mathcal F}\left(\sum_{i\in X}f_i+\sum_{j\in\mathcal D}\min_{i\in X}c_{ij}\right).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete, uncapacitated metric \(k\)-median with unit client weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given finite client and facility sets \(C\) and \(F\) in a metric space with distance \(d\), and an integer \(k\) satisfying \(1\le k\le |F|\), the metric \(k\)-median problem is
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{i\in C} d(i,S): S\subseteq F,\ |S|=k\right\},
\qquad d(i,S):=\min_{j\in S}d(i,j).
\]
An optimal set \(S^*\) is a metric \(k\)-median. Replacing \(|S|=k\) by \(|S|\le k\) gives the same optimal value because opening an additional facility cannot increase any nearest-facility distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select exactly k candidate facilities to minimize the sum of metric distances from clients to their nearest selected facilities.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric k-Median Location

children.title: Cardinality-Parameterized Median Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Alignment of the two cardinality-based naming conventions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(F\) are finite nonempty sets, with assignment costs \(c_{ij}\ge 0\).
The symbols \(p\) and \(k\) impose the same exact facility-cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{p\text{-median}}(C,F,c,p)=\operatorname{OPT}_{k\text{-median}}(C,F,c,k)\) whenever \(p=k\) and the remaining data coincide.

notation.meaning: Nearest open-facility cost for client i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: p-median and k-median are standard notational variants when their data and cardinality parameters coincide
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Notational correspondence for finite discrete uncapacitated median models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For identical client set \(C\), candidate set \(F\), and costs \((c_{ij})\), the discrete \(p\)-median and discrete \(k\)-median formulations correspond under the parameter substitution \(p=k\):
\[
\min_{S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p}\sum_{i\in C}\min_{j\in S}c_{ij}
=
\min_{S\subseteq F,\ |S|=k}\sum_{i\in C}\min_{j\in S}c_{ij}.
\]
Thus the two formulations have the same feasible facility sets, objective value for every feasible set, optimal value, and optimizers. The adjective metric adds the separate requirement that the costs arise from a metric; it is not implied by the cardinality correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With identical data and p equal to k, discrete p-median and k-median are the same optimization problem; metricity is an additional assumption.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Parameterized Median Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The p=k correspondence is precise and representation is the correct knowledge kind, but the claimed terminology correspondence lacks cited support.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(F\) are finite nonempty sets, and \(c_{ij}\ge 0\).
Each client has weight \(w_i\ge 0\), and \(1\le p\le |F|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p}\sum_{i\in C}w_i c(i,S)\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative demand or importance weight of client i.
Cost from client i to its nearest facility in S.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weighted median location uses a demand-weighted sum of nearest-facility costs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete weighted \(p\)-median without capacities or opening costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given client weights \(w_i\ge 0\), assignment costs \(c_{ij}\ge 0\), and a facility budget \(p\), weighted median location is
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{i\in C}w_i c(i,S):S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p\right\},
\qquad c(i,S):=\min_{j\in S}c_{ij}.
\]
A minimizer \(S^*\) is a weighted \(p\)-median. Clients with \(w_i=0\) do not affect the objective. Unit weights recover the unweighted discrete median model, while metric weighted median additionally requires the costs to be induced by a metric on the client and facility points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select p facilities to minimize the client-weighted sum of nearest-facility costs; unit weights recover ordinary discrete median location.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Median Location

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted discrete p-median definition is coherent and locally appropriate, but it has no supporting citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p}\sum_{r=1}^{n}\lambda_r c_{(r)}(S)\).

notation.meaning: Nearest-facility cost of client i under S.
The r-th smallest value among all client service costs.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: ordered-median location applies rank-dependent coefficients to sorted nearest-facility costs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ascending-order convention for a finite discrete ordered \(p\)-median.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each facility set \(S\subseteq F\), let \(c_i(S):=\min_{j\in S}c_{ij}\), and arrange these values in nondecreasing order as
\[
c_{(1)}(S)\le\cdots\le c_{(n)}(S).
\]
Given rank coefficients \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the ordered-median location problem is
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\lambda_r c_{(r)}(S):S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p\right\}.
\]
The ordering convention is part of the definition. Constant coefficients yield a median objective, while a coefficient supported on rank \(n\) yields a center objective when the remaining coefficients are zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort clients' nearest-facility costs and minimize a rank-weighted sum; particular rank coefficients recover median and center objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordered-Median Location

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ascending-order formulation is internally consistent, but ordered-median conventions and admissible rank coefficients vary; a specific authoritative source is required.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(F\) are finite nonempty sets, with costs \(c_{ij}\ge 0\) and weights \(w_i\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((S^*,O^*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{|S|=p,\ |O|\le z}\sum_{i\in C\setminus O}w_i c(i,S)\).

notation.meaning: Set of clients excluded as outliers.
Nearest open-facility cost of client i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: median with outliers jointly selects facilities and a bounded set of unserved clients
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-budget version of finite discrete weighted median with outliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Median location with at most \(z\) outliers jointly chooses an open-facility set \(S\) and an excluded-client set \(O\):
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{i\in C\setminus O}w_i c(i,S):S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p,\ O\subseteq C,\ |O|\le z\right\},
\qquad c(i,S):=\min_{j\in S}c_{ij}.
\]
Only clients in \(C\setminus O\) contribute to the service objective. A minimizer \((S^*,O^*)\) is a median solution with outliers. Setting \(z=0\) recovers weighted median location; using an outlier-weight budget instead would define a distinct variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose p facilities and exclude at most z clients so that the weighted service cost of all remaining clients is minimized.
knowledge_statements.title: Median Location with Outliers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cardinality-budget outlier model is coherent and fits the leaf, but the at-most-z convention and weighted formulation lack cited support.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(F\) are finite nonempty sets with service costs \(c_{ij}\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in F}\max_{i\in C}c_{ij}\), with radius \(R^*=\min_{j\in F}\max_{i\in C}c_{ij}\).

notation.meaning: Worst client service cost when facility j is selected.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the discrete one-center minimizes the maximum client-to-facility service cost
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete one-center; metricity is optional unless separately imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each candidate facility \(j\in F\), define its covering radius by
\[
R(j):=\max_{i\in C}c_{ij}.
\]
The discrete one-center problem is
\[
R^*:=\min_{j\in F}R(j)=\min_{j\in F}\max_{i\in C}c_{ij}.
\]
Any \(j^*\in F\) satisfying \(R(j^*)=R^*\) is a one-center. Equivalently, \(R^*\) is the smallest threshold \(R\) for which some candidate facility has \(c_{ij}\le R\) for every client \(i\in C\). If the costs are distances from a metric, this is the discrete metric one-center problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one candidate facility minimizing the largest service cost to any client; the optimum is the smallest radius covering every client.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Center

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The discrete one-center definition and threshold characterization are mathematically consistent, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: p-Center Location
children.top_down_role: Cardinality-constrained center location under the p-center convention.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(F\) are finite nonempty sets with service costs \(c_{ij}\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p}\max_{i\in C}c(i,S)\).

notation.meaning: Nearest open-facility cost of client i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: discrete p-center minimizes the maximum nearest-open-facility service cost under a cardinality constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete uncapacitated \(p\)-center with arbitrary nonnegative costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a facility set \(S\subseteq F\), define the service cost of client \(i\) and the induced radius by
\[
c(i,S):=\min_{j\in S}c_{ij},
\qquad R(S):=\max_{i\in C}c(i,S).
\]
The discrete \(p\)-center problem is
\[
\min\left\{R(S):S\subseteq F,\ |S|=p\right\}.
\]
An optimal set \(S^*\) is a \(p\)-center, and \(R(S^*)\) is its optimal covering radius. The formulation permits an arbitrary nonnegative client-facility cost matrix; requiring metric-induced costs gives the metric specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select p candidate facilities to minimize the largest cost incurred by any client when assigned to its nearest open facility.
knowledge_statements.title: p-Center Location

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The arbitrary-cost discrete p-center definition is coherent and correctly distinguished from its metric specialization, but it is uncited.

children.title: Metric k-Center Location
children.top_down_role: Center location under metric distances using the k-center convention.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(F\) are finite nonempty subsets of a metric space with distance \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq F,\ |S|=k}\max_{i\in C}d(i,S)\).

notation.meaning: Metric distance from client i to the nearest center in S.
Maximum client-to-center distance induced by S.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite metric k-center minimizes the maximum nearest-center metric distance under an exact cardinality constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete metric \(k\)-center with centers restricted to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a metric \(d\) on \(C\cup F\), define
\[
d(i,S):=\min_{j\in S}d(i,j),
\qquad R(S):=\max_{i\in C}d(i,S).
\]
The metric \(k\)-center problem is
\[
\min\left\{R(S):S\subseteq F,\ |S|=k\right\}.
\]
An optimizer \(S^*\) is a metric \(k\)-center, and \(R(S^*)\) is the least radius for which every client lies within that radius of some selected center. The restriction \(S\subseteq F\) distinguishes the discrete version from continuous center-location variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose k candidate centers minimizing the maximum metric distance from any client to its nearest chosen center.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric k-Center Location

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite discrete metric k-center definition is precise and fits the leaf, but no inspectable supporting citation is present.
